Here's how retrieval works in Ka-Ki-Gong, end to end.

## 1. Offline indexing (build-time)

 builds the index once (rerun anytime, cheap since the model tier is free):

1.  walks every `knowledge_base/<category>/schemes.json`, dedupes by `id` (a scheme like MediFund appears under multiple categories on SupportGoWhere) and merges the  list per scheme.
2. For each unique scheme,  pulls the **entire** Markdown page from `knowledge_base/<category>/md/*_{scheme_id}.md` as the  — one embedding per whole scheme document, not chunked (falls back to a reconstructed text from `schemes.json` if no `.md` file exists).
3.  embeds all  values via  (`nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b:free`), L2-normalizes the vectors, and saves everything to :
   -  — the raw NumPy matrix (no vector DB)
   - `schemes.json` — the deduplicated records
   -  — embedding model name, dim, count, timestamp

## 2. Runtime loading

At bot startup,  calls , which loads the matrix + records into memory and builds a  over the same  for lexical scoring. If the index files are missing, retrieval is skipped with a warning (bot still runs).

## 3. Deterministic per-turn retrieval (the main path)

This is the key design choice: retrieval does **not** wait for the LLM to call a tool. In `bot.py`:

- `_tag_latest_user_message_if_needed()` detects a new user message and calls `_update_retrieval_evidence(content)`.
- That function embeds the query via , then calls `scheme_index.search(...)`.
-  computes a **hybrid score**:
  $$\text{hybrid\_score} = \alpha \cdot \text{dense\_cosine} + (1-\alpha) \cdot \text{BM25}_{\text{norm}}$$
  where dense cosine comes from the normalized embedding dot product and BM25 is min-max normalized to `[0,1]` per query. Default `alpha=0.7` (`RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA`), `top_k=3` (`RETRIEVAL_TOP_K`), optional  filter and  threshold.
- Results are formatted by  into compact plain text (title, relevance score, description, up to 3 highlights, extracted "Phone number"/"How to apply"/"Where to go" sections stripped of Markdown links since it's spoken aloud, and source URL/date).
- This text is spliced into a `<retrieved_evidence>...</retrieved_evidence>` block inside the system prompt (see ) via regex replace, **before** the LLM call runs for that turn.

So every LLM turn is grounded in fresh evidence regardless of whether the model calls any tool.

## 4. Optional follow-up tool calling (off by default)

Two optional tools can be attached to `LLMContext(tools=[...])`:

- `search_senior_support` (), gated by `ENABLE_LLM_RETRIEVAL_TOOL` (default `False`) — lets the LLM re-query the same hybrid index mid-conversation, returning JSON via .
- `find_nearest_sso` (), gated by `ENABLE_SSO_LOOKUP_TOOL` (default `True`) — separate lookup over  via .

Both are disabled-by-default/documented as risky because of a known OpenRouter streaming-tool-call bug with `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on some upstream providers — the comments in `retrieval_tool.py` and `bot.py` explain this is why deterministic per-turn retrieval is the primary (non-tool-dependent) path.

## Summary diagram

#

"""Pipecat Quickstart — Voice bot.

Required AI services:
 - MERaLiON speech translation API (Hokkien audio → English text)
 - OpenRouter gpt-oss-120b (LLM) — served via OpenAI-compatible HTTP API
 - OpenRouter nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b:free (embeddings, for local retrieval)
 - MERaLiON-3-10B (Singapore Chinese renderer, enabled by default; see ENABLE_CHINESE_RENDERER)
 - OpenRouter qwen/qwen-audio-3.0-tts-flash (Text-to-Speech; Mandarin/English only, see services/openrouter_tts.py)

Run the bot using::

    uv run bots/bot.py

Before first run, build the retrieval index (see scripts/build_index.py)::

    uv run scripts/build_index.py

Pipeline::

    transport.input()
        ↓
    stt (MERaLiONSpeechTranslationService)
        ↓
    user_aggregator (LLMUserAggregator)
        ↓
    pre_llm_tagger (UserTurnPreLLMTagger)
        — also runs deterministic hybrid retrieval over knowledge_base/ and
          injects a <retrieved_evidence> block before every LLM call —
        ↓
    llm (OpenAILLMService → OpenRouter gpt-oss-120b)
        ↓
    chinese_renderer (ChineseRenderer → MERaLiON-3-10B)
        — buffers the complete English answer, renders it as Singapore
          Chinese, and keeps the verified English text in context —
        ↓
    tts (OpenRouterTTSService)
        ↓
    transport.output()
        ↓
    assistant_aggregator (LLMAssistantAggregator)
"""

import asyncio
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import aiohttp

# Ensure UTF-8 output on Windows (avoids UnicodeEncodeError for non-ASCII in logs).
if sys.platform == "win32":
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    sys.stderr.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

# Ensure the project root (pipecat-quickstart/) is on sys.path so local
# packages such as `processors/` are importable regardless of how the bot
# is launched (uv run, python -m, direct script invocation, etc.).
_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(_PROJECT_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_PROJECT_ROOT))

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from loguru import logger

print("Starting Pipecat bot...")
print("Loading models and imports (20 seconds, first run only)\n")

logger.info("Loading Silero VAD model...")
from pipecat.audio.vad.silero import SileroVADAnalyzer
from pipecat.audio.vad.vad_analyzer import VADParams

logger.info("✅ Silero VAD model loaded")

from pipecat.frames.frames import LLMRunFrame

logger.info("Loading pipeline components...")
from pipecat.pipeline.pipeline import Pipeline
from pipecat.pipeline.runner import PipelineRunner
from pipecat.pipeline.task import PipelineParams, PipelineTask
from pipecat.processors.aggregators.llm_context import LLMContext
from pipecat.processors.aggregators.llm_response_universal import (
    AssistantTurnStoppedMessage,
    LLMContextAggregatorPair,
    LLMUserAggregatorParams,
    UserTurnStoppedMessage,
)
from pipecat.processors.frame_processor import FrameDirection, FrameProcessor
from pipecat.runner.types import RunnerArguments
from pipecat.runner.utils import create_transport
from pipecat.services.openai.llm import OpenAILLMService
from pipecat.transports.base_transport import BaseTransport, TransportParams
from pipecat.turns.user_start import (
    TranscriptionUserTurnStartStrategy,
    VADUserTurnStartStrategy,
)
from pipecat.turns.user_stop import (
    SpeechTimeoutUserTurnStopStrategy,
)
from pipecat.turns.user_turn_strategies import UserTurnStrategies

from processors.retrieval_tool import format_evidence_block, make_search_senior_support_tool
from processors.sso_tool import make_find_nearest_sso_tool
from processors.chinese_renderer import ChineseRenderer
from retrieval.embeddings import OpenRouterEmbeddingClient
from retrieval.index import SchemeIndex
from retrieval.sso_lookup import SSODirectory
from services.meralion_speech_translation import MERaLiONSpeechTranslationService
from services.meralion_chinese_render import MERaLiONChineseRenderClient
from services.openrouter_tts import OpenRouterTTSService

if os.name != "nt":
    try:
        from pipecat.transports.daily.transport import DailyParams
    except ModuleNotFoundError:
        DailyParams = None
else:
    DailyParams = None

logger.info("✅ All components loaded successfully!")

ENV_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / ".env"
load_dotenv(dotenv_path=ENV_PATH, override=True)


def _env_float(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    raw_value = os.getenv(name)
    if raw_value is None:
        return default
    try:
        return float(raw_value)
    except ValueError:
        logger.warning("Invalid %s='%s'; falling back to %s", name, raw_value, default)
        return default


def _env_int(name: str, default: int | None = None) -> int | None:
    raw_value = os.getenv(name)
    if raw_value is None:
        return default
    try:
        return int(raw_value)
    except ValueError:
        logger.warning("Invalid %s='%s'; falling back to %s", name, raw_value, default)
        return default


def _env_optional_float(name: str) -> float | None:
    raw_value = os.getenv(name)
    if raw_value is None or not raw_value.strip():
        return None
    try:
        return float(raw_value)
    except ValueError:
        logger.warning("Invalid %s='%s'; ignoring value", name, raw_value)
        return None


def _env_bool(name: str, default: bool) -> bool:
    raw_value = os.getenv(name)
    if raw_value is None or not raw_value.strip():
        return default
    return raw_value.strip().lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on")


def _build_openrouter_settings() -> dict:
    """Collect generation parameters supported by OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible API."""
    settings: dict = {}

    temperature = _env_optional_float("OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE")
    if temperature is not None:
        settings["temperature"] = temperature

    top_p = _env_optional_float("OPENROUTER_TOP_P")
    if top_p is not None:
        settings["top_p"] = top_p

    max_tokens = _env_int("OPENROUTER_MAX_TOKENS")
    if max_tokens is not None:
        settings["max_tokens"] = max_tokens

    presence_penalty = _env_optional_float("OPENROUTER_PRESENCE_PENALTY")
    if presence_penalty is not None:
        settings["presence_penalty"] = presence_penalty

    frequency_penalty = _env_optional_float("OPENROUTER_FREQUENCY_PENALTY")
    if frequency_penalty is not None:
        settings["frequency_penalty"] = frequency_penalty

    reasoning_effort = (os.getenv("OPENROUTER_REASONING_EFFORT") or "low").strip()
    if reasoning_effort:
        # OpenRouter's chat-completions schema nests this under a "reasoning"
        # object (`{"reasoning": {"effort": ...}}`), not a flat top-level
        # "reasoning_effort" key — the latter is silently ignored, leaving
        # gpt-oss-120b at its provider-default (often "medium") reasoning
        # effort, which can add 30-45s of thinking time per turn. And since
        # "reasoning" isn't a param the OpenAI SDK's create() recognizes
        # either, it must be passed via extra_body so the SDK forwards it
        # unvalidated instead of raising "unexpected keyword argument".
        settings["extra"] = {"extra_body": {"reasoning": {"effort": reasoning_effort}}}

    return settings


def _resolve_system_prompt() -> str:
    system_prompt_file = (os.getenv("OPENROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE") or "").strip()
    inline_prompt = (os.getenv("OPENROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT") or "").strip()

    if system_prompt_file:
        prompt_path = Path(system_prompt_file).expanduser()
        if not prompt_path.is_absolute():
            prompt_path = (ENV_PATH.parent / prompt_path).resolve()

        try:
            prompt_from_file = prompt_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
        except OSError as exc:
            logger.warning(
                "Unable to load OPENROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE='{}': {}",
                prompt_path,
                exc,
            )
            return inline_prompt

        if not prompt_from_file:
            logger.warning(
                "OPENROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE='{}' is empty; falling back to OPENROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT",
                prompt_path,
            )
            return inline_prompt

        if inline_prompt:
            logger.warning(
                "Both OPENROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FILE and OPENROUTER_SYSTEM_PROMPT are set; using file prompt"
            )

        logger.info("Loaded system prompt from file: {}", prompt_path)
        return prompt_from_file

    return inline_prompt


def _load_render_prompt_template(relative_path: str) -> str:
    """Load the MERaLiON-3-10B Chinese-renderer prompt template from disk."""
    prompt_path = Path(relative_path).expanduser()
    if not prompt_path.is_absolute():
        prompt_path = (ENV_PATH.parent / prompt_path).resolve()
    return prompt_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


async def run_bot(transport: BaseTransport, runner_args: RunnerArguments):
    logger.info("Starting bot")
    logger.info("Loaded env from: {}", ENV_PATH)

    aiohttp_session = aiohttp.ClientSession()

    openrouter_api_key = os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"]
    openrouter_base_url = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_BASE_URL", "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1")
    openrouter_model = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_MODEL", "openai/gpt-oss-120b")
    logger.info("Using OpenRouter model: {} @ {}", openrouter_model, openrouter_base_url)
    openrouter_settings = _build_openrouter_settings()
    logger.info("OpenRouter generation settings: {}", openrouter_settings)
    openrouter_tts_model = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TTS_MODEL", "qwen/qwen-audio-3.0-tts-flash")
    openrouter_tts_voice = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TTS_VOICE", "longanhuan_v3.6")
    system_prompt = _resolve_system_prompt()
    if system_prompt:
        logger.info("Custom system prompt enabled")

    user_turn_count = 0
    _last_counted_msg_index: int = -1
    _conversation_started = False
    vad_stop_secs = _env_float("VAD_STOP_SECS", 0.8)
    user_turn_stop_timeout = _env_float("USER_TURN_STOP_TIMEOUT", 10.0)
    user_speech_timeout = _env_float("USER_SPEECH_TIMEOUT", 4.5)

    meralion_api_key = os.environ["MERALION_API_KEY"]
    meralion_base_url = os.getenv("MERALION_API_BASE_URL", "https://api.meralion.ai")
    meralion_translation_model = os.getenv(
        "MERALION_TRANSLATION_MODEL", "MERaLiON/MERaLiON-3-3B-ASR-CTM"
    )
    logger.info(
        "Using MERaLiON speech translation model: {} @ {}",
        meralion_translation_model,
        meralion_base_url,
    )
    stt = MERaLiONSpeechTranslationService(
        api_key=meralion_api_key,
        base_url=meralion_base_url,
        model=meralion_translation_model,
    )

    # --- MERaLiON-3-10B Singapore Chinese renderer -------------------------------
    # Narrow transformation only (STREAMLINED_PIPELINE_CONTEXT.md section 3.5):
    # verified grounded English answer -> Singapore Chinese. Runs on the
    # complete buffered LLM response (see processors/chinese_renderer.py) so no
    # partial English fragments ever reach the renderer or the TTS model.
    enable_chinese_renderer = _env_bool("ENABLE_CHINESE_RENDERER", True)
    chinese_renderer: ChineseRenderer | None = None
    chinese_render_client: MERaLiONChineseRenderClient | None = None
    if enable_chinese_renderer:
        render_prompt_file = os.getenv(
            "MERALION_RENDER_PROMPT_FILE", "prompt/english_to_singapore-chinese.md"
        )
        render_model = os.getenv("MERALION_RENDER_MODEL", "MERaLiON/MERaLiON-3-10B")
        logger.info(
            "Using MERaLiON Singapore Chinese renderer model: {} @ {} (prompt={})",
            render_model,
            meralion_base_url,
            render_prompt_file,
        )
        chinese_render_client = MERaLiONChineseRenderClient(
            api_key=meralion_api_key,
            prompt_template=_load_render_prompt_template(render_prompt_file),
            base_url=meralion_base_url,
            model=render_model,
            temperature=_env_float("MERALION_RENDER_TEMPERATURE", 0.2),
        )
        chinese_renderer = ChineseRenderer(chinese_render_client)
    else:
        logger.warning(
            "ENABLE_CHINESE_RENDERER=false: grounded English answers are sent "
            "directly to the TTS model, skipping the MERaLiON-3-10B "
            "Hanji-rendering step."
        )

    logger.info("Using OpenRouter TTS model: {} (voice={})", openrouter_tts_model, openrouter_tts_voice)
    tts = OpenRouterTTSService(
        api_key=os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TTS_API_KEY") or openrouter_api_key,
        aiohttp_session=aiohttp_session,
        base_url=os.getenv("OPENROUTER_TTS_BASE_URL", openrouter_base_url),
        model=openrouter_tts_model,
        voice=openrouter_tts_voice,
        pcm_sample_rate=_env_int("OPENROUTER_TTS_PCM_SAMPLE_RATE", 24000),
    )

    # --- Local retrieval over the curated SupportGoWhere knowledge base ---------
    # Retrieval-first policy (STREAMLINED_PIPELINE_CONTEXT.md section 2/8): evidence
    # is fetched deterministically for every user turn (see
    # `_update_retrieval_evidence` below) rather than via LLM tool calling, so the
    # grounded-answer call never depends on gpt-oss-120b successfully emitting a
    # tool call.
    retrieval_data_dir = _PROJECT_ROOT / os.getenv("RETRIEVAL_DATA_DIR", "data")
    retrieval_top_k = _env_int("RETRIEVAL_TOP_K", 3)
    retrieval_min_score = _env_float("RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE", 0.0)
    retrieval_alpha = _env_float("RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA", 0.7)
    enable_llm_retrieval_tool = _env_bool("ENABLE_LLM_RETRIEVAL_TOOL", False)
    enable_sso_lookup_tool = _env_bool("ENABLE_SSO_LOOKUP_TOOL", True)

    embed_client = OpenRouterEmbeddingClient(
        api_key=openrouter_api_key,
        base_url=openrouter_base_url,
        model=os.getenv("OPENROUTER_EMBEDDING_MODEL", "nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b:free"),
        query_prefix=os.getenv("OPENROUTER_EMBED_QUERY_PREFIX", ""),
        passage_prefix=os.getenv("OPENROUTER_EMBED_PASSAGE_PREFIX", ""),
    )

    scheme_index: SchemeIndex | None = None
    try:
        scheme_index = SchemeIndex.load(retrieval_data_dir)
        logger.info(
            "Loaded retrieval index: {} schemes (embedding_model={})",
            scheme_index.scheme_count,
            scheme_index.manifest.get("embedding_model"),
        )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        logger.warning(
            "No retrieval index found at {}. Run `uv run scripts/build_index.py` "
            "first — retrieval will be skipped until then.",
            retrieval_data_dir,
        )

    llm = OpenAILLMService(
        api_key=openrouter_api_key,
        base_url=openrouter_base_url,
        model=openrouter_model,
        params=OpenAILLMService.InputParams(**openrouter_settings) if openrouter_settings else None,
    )

    tools = []
    if enable_llm_retrieval_tool and scheme_index is not None:
        tools.append(
            make_search_senior_support_tool(
                scheme_index,
                embed_client,
                top_k=retrieval_top_k,
                min_score=retrieval_min_score,
                alpha=retrieval_alpha,
            )
        )
        logger.warning(
            "ENABLE_LLM_RETRIEVAL_TOOL=true: follow-up tool calling is enabled on "
            "openai/gpt-oss-120b via OpenRouter. This model has a documented "
            "broken-streaming-tool-call issue on at least one OpenRouter upstream "
            "provider (see processors/retrieval_tool.py). Deterministic per-turn "
            "retrieval remains active regardless of this setting."
        )

    if enable_sso_lookup_tool:
        sso_locations_path = _PROJECT_ROOT / os.getenv(
            "SSO_LOCATIONS_FILE", "knowledge_base/social_service_offices/sso_locations.json"
        )
        sso_directory = SSODirectory.load(sso_locations_path)
        tools.append(make_find_nearest_sso_tool(sso_directory))
        logger.info("find_nearest_sso tool enabled (data: {})", sso_locations_path)
        logger.warning(
            "ENABLE_SSO_LOOKUP_TOOL=true: follow-up tool calling is enabled on "
            "openai/gpt-oss-120b via OpenRouter, which has a documented "
            "broken-streaming-tool-call issue on at least one OpenRouter upstream "
            "provider (see processors/retrieval_tool.py). Set ENABLE_SSO_LOOKUP_TOOL=false "
            "if find_nearest_sso calls fail to stream correctly."
        )

    context = LLMContext(tools=tools) if tools else LLMContext()
    user_aggregator, assistant_aggregator = LLMContextAggregatorPair(
        context,
        user_params=LLMUserAggregatorParams(
            vad_analyzer=SileroVADAnalyzer(params=VADParams(stop_secs=vad_stop_secs)),
            user_turn_stop_timeout=user_turn_stop_timeout,
            user_turn_strategies=UserTurnStrategies(
                start=[VADUserTurnStartStrategy(), TranscriptionUserTurnStartStrategy()],
                stop=[
                    SpeechTimeoutUserTurnStopStrategy(
                        user_speech_timeout=user_speech_timeout,
                    )
                ],
            ),
        ),
    )

    logger.info(
        "Turn detection config | vad_stop_secs={} | user_speech_timeout={} | user_turn_stop_timeout={}",
        vad_stop_secs,
        user_speech_timeout,
        user_turn_stop_timeout,
    )

    def _update_system_turn_metadata(turn: int) -> None:
        """Atomically replace the live <session_state> block with updated user_turn.

        Uses a regex that only matches <session_state> with NO attributes, so it
        never touches the <session_state at="example-N"> blocks in the few-shot
        examples section.
        """
        _live_re = re.compile(r'<session_state>(.*?)</session_state>', re.DOTALL)
        messages = context.get_messages()
        for i in range(len(messages)):
            if messages[i].get("role") == "system":
                content = messages[i]["content"]
                m = _live_re.search(content)
                if m:
                    new_block = (
                        f"<session_state>"
                        f"\n  <user_turn>{turn}</user_turn>"
                        f"\n</session_state>"
                    )
                    messages[i]["content"] = _live_re.sub(new_block, content, count=1)
                else:
                    new_block = (
                        f"<session_state>"

"""Formatting helpers and the optional follow-up ``search_senior_support`` tool.

Per STREAMLINED_PIPELINE_CONTEXT.md section 8:

- Initial-turn policy: retrieval runs deterministically (no LLM/tool call).
- Follow-up policy: the LLM *may* call ``search_senior_support`` again if it
  decides it needs new evidence.

See ``bots/bot.py`` for why the follow-up tool is gated behind
``ENABLE_LLM_RETRIEVAL_TOOL`` (default off): Pipecat's own CHANGELOG documents
a broken-streaming-tool-call bug specific to ``openai/gpt-oss-120b`` through at
least one OpenRouter upstream (Nebius) as of v1.4.0, and a related class of
"tool_call id/name split across deltas" bugs affecting other OpenAI-compatible
providers (pipecat-ai/pipecat#4987). OpenRouter can route this model to
several different backing providers, and Pipecat has no way to know in
advance which one will serve a given request, so this failure mode cannot be
ruled out reliably. The deterministic per-turn retrieval below does not
depend on tool calling at all and is the safe default.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from retrieval.index import SchemeIndex
from retrieval.schemas import RetrievedScheme

_MD_LINK_RE = re.compile(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]+\)")


def _strip_markdown_links(text: str) -> str:
    """Drop [label](url) -> label; evidence is read aloud, not clicked."""
    return _MD_LINK_RE.sub(r"\1", text)


def _extract_section(embedding_text: str, heading: str) -> str:
    """Pull one '## {heading}' section out of a scheme's embedding_text blob."""
    pattern = re.compile(rf"##\s*{re.escape(heading)}\s*\n(.*?)(?=\n##\s|\Z)", re.DOTALL)
    match = pattern.search(embedding_text)
    if not match:
        return ""
    return _strip_markdown_links(match.group(1)).strip()


def format_evidence_block(results: list[RetrievedScheme]) -> str:
    """Render retrieved schemes as compact evidence for the grounded-answer LLM turn."""
    if not results:
        return "No verified scheme evidence was found for this turn."

    lines = []
    for i, result in enumerate(results, start=1):
        scheme = result.scheme
        lines.append(f"{i}. {scheme.title} (relevance={result.hybrid_score:.2f})")
        if scheme.description:
            lines.append(f"   Summary: {scheme.description}")
        for highlight in scheme.highlights[:3]:
            lines.append(f"   - {highlight}")

        phone = _extract_section(scheme.embedding_text, "Phone number")
        if phone:
            lines.append(f"   Phone number: {phone}")

        how_to_apply = _extract_section(scheme.embedding_text, "How to apply?")
        if how_to_apply:
            lines.append(f"   How to apply: {how_to_apply}")

        where_to_go = _extract_section(scheme.embedding_text, "Where to go")
        if where_to_go:
            lines.append(f"   Where to go: {where_to_go}")

        updated = scheme.source_updated_at or "unknown"
        lines.append(f"   Source: {scheme.source_url} (last updated: {updated})")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def format_tool_result(results: list[RetrievedScheme]) -> dict:
    """Shape retrieved schemes into the tool-result JSON from section 8 of the spec."""
    return {
        "results": [
            {
                "scheme_id": result.scheme.scheme_id,
                "title": result.scheme.title,
                "relevant_passage": result.scheme.description,
                "source_url": result.scheme.source_url,
                "source_updated_at": result.scheme.source_updated_at,
                "retrieval_score": round(result.hybrid_score, 4),
            }
            for result in results
        ],
        "retrieval_confident": bool(results) and results[0].hybrid_score >= 0.5,
    }


def make_search_senior_support_tool(
    index: SchemeIndex,
    embed_client,
    *,
    top_k: int = 3,
    min_score: float = 0.0,
    alpha: float = 0.7,
):
    """Build the direct-function tool handler for follow-up retrieval.

    Returns an async function suitable for ``LLMContext(tools=[...])`` — Pipecat
    derives the tool's JSON schema from this function's signature and docstring
    (see the "direct functions" pattern in Pipecat's function-calling docs).
    """

    async def search_senior_support(params, query: str, category: str | None = None):
        """Search verified Singapore senior-support scheme records.

        Args:
            query: A concise English description of the user's support need.
            category: Optional category such as healthcare, caregiving, mobility,
                financial_support, or long_term_care.
        """
        query_embedding = await embed_client.embed_query(query)
        results = index.search(
            query,
            query_embedding,
            top_k=top_k,
            min_score=min_score,
            category=category,
            alpha=alpha,
        )
        await params.result_callback(format_tool_result(results))

    return search_senior_support

a phone number to call, or a place to physically go to.

  by an upstream speech-translation service. Treat it as what the user said,
  even if the wording is imperfect.

  turn by local hybrid (dense + lexical) search over a curated snapshot of
  SupportGoWhere scheme pages. It lists the top matching schemes with a short
  summary, highlights, and — when available — how to apply, where to go, a

Your reply is spoken aloud almost immediately by a Singapore Chinese
rendering step and then a text-to-speech model. Because of this:

- Return plain spoken English prose only. No Markdown, no JSON, no bullet
  points, no headings, no labels, no code fences.
- No more than three short sentences.

3. Do not infer the user's age, citizenship, income, diagnosis, disability,

8. Give exactly one practical next step, and prefer this order of

## openrouter-api-gotchas.md
# OpenRouter API gotchas

- Reasoning effort control uses a **nested** top-level `reasoning` object:
  `{"reasoning": {"effort": "low"}}`. A flat `"reasoning_effort": "low"` key
  is NOT a valid OpenRouter param and is silently ignored — the model falls
  back to its provider default effort (often "medium"), which can add
  30-45s of hidden "thinking" latency per turn for reasoning models like
  `openai/gpt-oss-120b`. Symptom: huge `processing time` in Pipecat logs with
  high `reasoning tokens` in usage metrics, looks like the pipeline is "stuck".
  - Valid `effort` values: max, xhigh, high, medium, low, minimal, none.
  - Pipecat's `OpenAILLMService.InputParams(extra={...})` merges `extra` keys
    directly into the kwargs passed to the openai SDK's
    `client.chat.completions.create(**params)`. The SDK's `create()` method
    only recognizes its own documented kwargs — passing `reasoning` directly
    raises `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'reasoning'`, since that's
    an OpenRouter-only extension, not part of the OpenAI SDK's method
    signature. The correct fix is to nest it inside `extra_body` (a kwarg the
    SDK *does* recognize and forwards unvalidated into the JSON body):
    `extra={"extra_body": {"reasoning": {"effort": "low"}}}`.
- For latency-sensitive voice/chat bots using reasoning-capable models via
  OpenRouter, always set an explicit low reasoning effort — don't rely on
  provider defaults.

toolCallRounds.response:
Here's how retrieval works in Ka-Ki-Gong, end to end.

## 1. Offline indexing (build-time)

[scripts/build_index.py](scripts/build_index.py) builds the index once (rerun anytime, cheap since the model tier is free):

1. [load_records()](retrieval/index.py#L67-L98) walks every `knowledge_base/<category>/schemes.json`, dedupes by `id` (a scheme like MediFund appears under multiple categories on SupportGoWhere) and merges the `categories` list per scheme.
2. For each unique scheme, [_find_md_text()](retrieval/index.py#L57-L63) pulls the **entire** Markdown page from `knowledge_base/<category>/md/*_{scheme_id}.md` as the `embedding_text` — one embedding per whole scheme document, not chunked (falls back to a reconstructed text from `schemes.json` if no `.md` file exists).
3. [SchemeIndex.build()](retrieval/index.py#L124-L138) embeds all `embedding_text` values via [OpenRouterEmbeddingClient.embed_passages()](retrieval/embeddings.py#L59-L62) (`nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b:free`), L2-normalizes the vectors, and saves everything to `data/`:
   - `embeddings.npy` — the raw NumPy matrix (no vector DB)
   - `schemes.json` — the deduplicated records
   - `manifest.json` — embedding model name, dim, count, timestamp

## 2. Runtime loading

At bot startup, [bot.py](bots/bot.py) calls `SchemeIndex.load(retrieval_data_dir)`, which loads the matrix + records into memory and builds a [BM25Index](retrieval/lexical.py#L29-L84) over the same `embedding_text` for lexical scoring. If the index files are missing, retrieval is skipped with a warning (bot still runs).

## 3. Deterministic per-turn retrieval (the main path)

This is the key design choice: retrieval does **not** wait for the LLM to call a tool. In `bot.py`:

- `_tag_latest_user_message_if_needed()` detects a new user message and calls `_update_retrieval_evidence(content)`.
- That function embeds the query via `embed_client.embed_query()`, then calls `scheme_index.search(...)`.
- [SchemeIndex.search()](retrieval/index.py#L163-L196) computes a **hybrid score**:
  $$\text{hybrid\_score} = \alpha \cdot \text{dense\_cosine} + (1-\alpha) \cdot \text{BM25}_{\text{norm}}$$
  where dense cosine comes from the normalized embedding dot product and BM25 is min-max normalized to `[0,1]` per query. Default `alpha=0.7` (`RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA`), `top_k=3` (`RETRIEVAL_TOP_K`), optional `category` filter and `min_score` threshold.
- Results are formatted by [format_evidence_block()](processors/retrieval_tool.py#L37-L64) into compact plain text (title, relevance score, description, up to 3 highlights, extracted "Phone number"/"How to apply"/"Where to go" sections stripped of Markdown links since it's spoken aloud, and source URL/date).
- This text is spliced into a `<retrieved_evidence>...</retrieved_evidence>` block inside the system prompt (see [PROMPT_TEMPLATE_senior_support_grounded_answer.md](prompt/PROMPT_TEMPLATE_senior_support_grounded_answer.md)) via regex replace, **before** the LLM call runs for that turn.

So every LLM turn is grounded in fresh evidence regardless of whether the model calls any tool.

## 4. Optional follow-up tool calling (off by default)

Two optional tools can be attached to `LLMContext(tools=[...])`:

- `search_senior_support` ([make_search_senior_support_tool()](processors/retrieval_tool.py#L86-L109)), gated by `ENABLE_LLM_RETRIEVAL_TOOL` (default `False`) — lets the LLM re-query the same hybrid index mid-conversation, returning JSON via [format_tool_result()](processors/retrieval_tool.py#L67-L82).
- `find_nearest_sso` ([processors/sso_tool.py](processors/sso_tool.py)), gated by `ENABLE_SSO_LOOKUP_TOOL` (default `True`) — separate lookup over `knowledge_base/social_service_offices/sso_locations.json` via [retrieval/sso_lookup.py](retrieval/sso_lookup.py).

Both are disabled-by-default/documented as risky because of a known OpenRouter streaming-tool-call bug with `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on some upstream providers — the comments in `retrieval_tool.py` and `bot.py` explain this is why deterministic per-turn retrieval is the primary (non-tool-dependent) path.

## Summary diagram

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[knowledge_base/*/schemes.json + md/] -->|build_index.py, offline| B[data/embeddings.npy + schemes.json + manifest.json]
    B -->|SchemeIndex.load at startup| C[In-memory SchemeIndex]
    D[User turn text] --> E[embed_client.embed_query]
    E --> F[SchemeIndex.search: hybrid dense+BM25]
    C --> F
    F --> G[format_evidence_block]
    G --> H["<retrieved_evidence> spliced into system prompt"]
    H --> I[LLM call - grounded answer]
    D -.optional tool call.-> J[search_senior_support / find_nearest_sso]
    J -.-> F
```

Notes on this format (from [format_evidence_block()](processors/retrieval_tool.py#L37-L64)):
- `Summary` and highlights come from `schemes.json`, not the `.md` file.
- `Phone number`/`How to apply`/`Where to go` are extracted verbatim from the scheme's `## Heading` sections in its `.md` file via regex ([_extract_section()](processors/retrieval_tool.py#L21-L26)), with `[label](url)` markdown links stripped down to just `label` (since it's spoken, not clicked).
- Result 3 (CAREwell) has no `## Phone number` section in its `.md` file, so that line is simply omitted — this is why the prompt template has rule 8c telling the LLM to fall back to a physical address or a general hotline when no phone number is present in the evidence.
- `last updated: unknown` appears when `info_last_updated` is null in `schemes.json`.

Both — they serve different roles:

**`schemes.json`** (per category) provides the **structured metadata** for each `SchemeRecord`:
- `title`, `description`, `categories`, `domains`, `profiles`, `highlights`, `source_url` (`url`), `source_updated_at` (`info_last_updated`)
- This is what [load_records()](retrieval/index.py#L67-L98) reads to build every record, and it's also what dedupes/merges `categories` when the same scheme ID appears in multiple category folders.

**`md/*.md`** provides the **embedding text** — the actual content that gets vectorized:
- [_find_md_text()](retrieval/index.py#L57-L63) looks for a file matching `*_{scheme_id}.md` in that category's `md/` folder and uses its full contents as `embedding_text`.
- If no matching `.md` file exists, [_fallback_embedding_text()](retrieval/index.py#L44-L51) reconstructs a Markdown-ish text from the `schemes.json` fields instead (title + description + highlights + sections) — so every scheme always has *some* embedding text, `.md` or not.
- `embedding_text` is also what BM25 indexes for the lexical half of hybrid search, and what [_extract_section()](processors/retrieval_tool.py#L21-L26) parses at evidence-formatting time to pull out `## Phone number`, `## How to apply?`, `## Where to go` for the evidence block.

So at query time: the dense score comes from embedding the `.md` content (or its fallback), the lexical/BM25 score comes from the same text, and the final evidence block for the LLM mixes `schemes.json` fields (`Summary`, highlights) with `.md`-extracted sections (`Phone number`, `How to apply`, `Where to go`).

"""Data structures shared by the retrieval package."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class SchemeRecord:
    """One scheme, embedded as a single whole-document passage.

    ``scheme_id`` is deduplicated across ``knowledge_base/<category>/`` folders:
    the same scheme (e.g. MediFund) commonly appears under several categories on
    SupportGoWhere, so ``categories`` collects every folder it was found in
    while the record itself is stored once.
    """

    scheme_id: str
    title: str
    description: str
    categories: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    domains: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    profiles: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    highlights: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    source_url: str = ""
    source_updated_at: str | None = None
    embedding_text: str = ""
    """Full Markdown content that was embedded (one embedding per scheme)."""

    def to_json(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "scheme_id": self.scheme_id,
            "title": self.title,
            "description": self.description,
            "categories": self.categories,
            "domains": self.domains,
            "profiles": self.profiles,
            "highlights": self.highlights,
            "source_url": self.source_url,
            "source_updated_at": self.source_updated_at,
            "embedding_text": self.embedding_text,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, data: dict) -> "SchemeRecord":
        return cls(
            scheme_id=data["scheme_id"],
            title=data.get("title", ""),
            description=data.get("description", ""),
            categories=data.get("categories", []),
            domains=data.get("domains", []),
            profiles=data.get("profiles", []),
            highlights=data.get("highlights", []),
            source_url=data.get("source_url", ""),
            source_updated_at=data.get("source_updated_at"),
            embedding_text=data.get("embedding_text", ""),
        )


@dataclass
class RetrievedScheme:
    """A scheme returned by hybrid search, with its component scores."""

    scheme: SchemeRecord
    dense_score: float
    lexical_score: float
    hybrid_score: float

toolCallRounds.response:
No LLM involved anywhere in this pipeline — it's fully deterministic scraping + field mapping. Two separate stages produced these fields:

## 1. Where the fields came from: the scraper

[scripts/scrape_supportgowhere_schemes.py](scripts/scrape_supportgowhere_schemes.py) calls SupportGoWhere's own public JSON APIs (a Singapore gov site) directly — a list API per domain/topic and a detail API per scheme/service. [normalize_detail()](scripts/scrape_supportgowhere_schemes.py#L149-L172) maps the **site's own API response fields** 1:1 into a flat dict:

```python
"id": summary["id"], "title": ..., "description": ...,
"domains": _simplify_ref_list(detail.get("domains")),
"profiles": _simplify_ref_list(detail.get("profiles")),
"highlights": detail.get("highlights") or [],
"info_last_updated": detail.get("infoLastUpdated"),
```

So `domains`, `profiles`, `highlights`, `info_last_updated`, `description`, `keywords` etc. aren't invented — they're whatever SupportGoWhere itself tags each scheme with. `sections` (About this support / Who is this for / How to apply / Where to go / Phone number / etc.) come from [FIELD_LABELS](scripts/scrape_supportgowhere_schemes.py#L54-L64), a hand-picked mapping of the API's rich-text field keys (`howToApply`, `address`, `phoneNumber`...) to human-readable headings — a deliberate author choice, but still just relabeling the site's own fields, not extracting/summarizing them with a model. The rich text itself is TipTap ProseMirror JSON, deterministically converted to Markdown by [tiptap_to_markdown()](scripts/scrape_supportgowhere_schemes.py#L145-L151) (a hand-written recursive renderer, [_render_block()](scripts/scrape_supportgowhere_schemes.py#L120-L134)/[_render_inline()](scripts/scrape_supportgowhere_schemes.py#L104-L118)).

This produces `knowledge_base/<topic>/schemes.json` (the flat dicts) and one `.md` file per scheme (rendered via [to_markdown_doc()](scripts/scrape_supportgowhere_schemes.py#L154-L177)).

## 2. Why `SchemeRecord` looks different from `schemes.json`

`SchemeRecord` in [retrieval/schemas.py](retrieval/schemas.py) is a **narrower, retrieval-purpose-built subset** of the scraped `schemes.json` entry, assembled by [load_records()](retrieval/index.py#L67-L98):

| `SchemeRecord` field | Source |
|---|---|
| `scheme_id`, `title`, `description`, `domains`, `profiles`, `highlights`, `source_url` (← `url`), `source_updated_at` (← `info_last_updated`) | Copied straight from `schemes.json` |
| `categories` | Not in `schemes.json` at all — derived from *which topic folder(s)* the scheme appeared under, accumulated across folders during dedup (a scheme can be tagged in multiple `knowledge_base/<category>/` dirs) |
| `embedding_text` | Not in `schemes.json` — read from the sibling `.md` file (or reconstructed from the JSON fields via [_fallback_embedding_text()](retrieval/index.py#L44-L51) if no `.md` exists) |

Fields present in scraped `schemes.json` but **dropped** from `SchemeRecord` (because retrieval doesn't need them): `type`, `keywords`, `citizenship`, `min_age`, `max_age`, `cost`, `sections` (the raw section dict — superseded by `embedding_text` + the runtime regex extraction in `retrieval_tool.py`).

So the design lineage is: **gov API schema → scraper's chosen field subset (`schemes.json`/`.md`) → retrieval's chosen field subset (`SchemeRecord`)** — each stage a deliberate, code-visible trim, never an LLM inferring or extracting anything.

From each `RetrievedScheme` (a `SchemeRecord` + its 3 scores), only this subset is rendered into the `<retrieved_evidence>` text ([processors/retrieval_tool.py](processors/retrieval_tool.py#L37-L64)):

Worth thinking through before changing it — there are real tradeoffs given how this bot is built.

## Why the current design deliberately doesn't do this

1. **Latency.** Your own `.env` comments and prompt design show latency is a first-class constraint here (`VAD_STOP_SECS`, `OPENROUTER_REASONING_EFFORT=low` explicitly to avoid 30-45s of added thinking time). Dumping the full `embedding_text` for top-3 results means re-sending 3× a full scheme page (each `.md` runs ~40-90 lines including boilerplate) into the system prompt on *every single turn* — this inflates prompt size substantially, which increases prefill/time-to-first-token in a voice pipeline where every second is noticeable to the caller.
2. **Noise the LLM shouldn't act on.** The full `.md` includes sections the prompt's Output Contract explicitly forbids surfacing — `Agency website`, `Email / Form` (both raw URLs), and full `Who is this for?` eligibility criteria text. Rule 2/3 of your prompt already fight to stop the model from asserting eligibility or inferring citizenship/age/income; handing it the raw eligibility clauses (e.g. "Monthly per capita household income ≤ $4,800") makes it *more* tempting for the model to reason about whether the caller qualifies and assert something it shouldn't, not less.
3. **It contradicts the stated design intent.** `format_evidence_block()`'s docstring literally says "compact evidence for the grounded-answer LLM turn" — the 3-highlight cap and the 3-field extraction (phone/how-to-apply/where-to-go) were a deliberate choice to keep evidence to only what's actionable over voice, matching the "exactly one practical next step" rule (#8) in the prompt.

## Where full-md *would* genuinely help

If you're seeing the model give vague or wrong "what this scheme covers" answers because `description` + 3 highlights isn't enough substance, the actual gap is probably **`About this support`** (the fuller explanation) — not literally everything.

## Suggested middle ground

Rather than the raw dump, extract 1-2 more deterministic sections the same way phone/how-to-apply/where-to-go already are:
- Add `About this support` (full explanatory body) to the evidence block.
- Optionally raise `highlights[:3]` to `highlights[:5]`.
- Still skip `Agency website`, `Email / Form`, and raw `Who is this for?` criteria — those either aren't voice-appropriate or invite eligibility over-reach.

Want me to implement that (add an `About this support` extraction into [format_evidence_block()](processors/retrieval_tool.py#L37-L64)), or do you specifically want the truly-full raw `.md` regardless of the tradeoffs above?

    """Render retrieved schemes as evidence for the grounded-answer LLM turn.

    Includes every scraped section (not just phone/how-to-apply/where-to-go) so

# Ka-Ki-Gong: Hokkien Voice Access to Singapore Senior Support Schemes

Ka-Ki-Gong ("speak for yourself" in Hokkien) is a voice assistant prototype that
helps Singapore Hokkien-speaking seniors discover and understand caregiving and
senior-support schemes. A spoken Hokkien question is translated to English,
answered using a curated, locally-retrieved snapshot of
[SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/) scheme pages, and spoken
back in Singapore Chinese through a cloud text-to-speech model.

This is an accessibility research prototype, not an official integration with
SupportGoWhere, LifeSG, GovTech, MSF, MOH, AIC, or any other government agency.
It does not confirm eligibility or submit applications. See
[STREAMLINED_PIPELINE_CONTEXT.md](STREAMLINED_PIPELINE_CONTEXT.md) for the full
design specification this implementation follows.

## Status

**Implemented and wired into `bots/bot.py`:**

- Hokkien (or other supported language) speech → English text, via the
  MERaLiON speech-translation API ([services/meralion_speech_translation.py](services/meralion_speech_translation.py))
- Local hybrid retrieval (dense + lexical) over 303 curated SupportGoWhere
  scheme records in [knowledge_base/](knowledge_base/), run deterministically
  before every turn ([retrieval/](retrieval/), [processors/retrieval_tool.py](processors/retrieval_tool.py))
- Grounded English answer generation via `openai/gpt-oss-120b` through
  OpenRouter, with retrieved evidence injected into the system prompt each turn
- MERaLiON-3-10B English → Singapore Chinese rendering, run once per complete
  buffered assistant turn before TTS
  ([services/meralion_chinese_render.py](services/meralion_chinese_render.py),
  [processors/chinese_renderer.py](processors/chinese_renderer.py),
  [prompt/english_to_singapore-chinese.md](prompt/english_to_singapore-chinese.md)).
  The verified English answer is still what's stored in conversation context;
  only the spoken output is rendered as Singapore Chinese. Toggle with
  `ENABLE_CHINESE_RENDERER` (default `true`; set to `false` to send the
  grounded English answer directly to TTS as before).
- Text-to-speech via OpenRouter's `qwen/qwen-audio-3.0-tts-flash`
  ([services/openrouter_tts.py](services/openrouter_tts.py)). Note: this
  model's system voices only cover Mandarin Chinese and English — there is no
  Hokkien/Minnan voice, so spoken output is Mandarin-pronounced Singapore
  Chinese, not Hokkien.
- Optional `find_nearest_sso` follow-up tool
  ([processors/sso_tool.py](processors/sso_tool.py),
  [retrieval/sso_lookup.py](retrieval/sso_lookup.py)) that looks up the
  Social Service Office nearest an area the user names, from a transcribed
  MSF contact list
  ([knowledge_base/social_service_offices/](knowledge_base/social_service_offices/)).
  Toggle with `ENABLE_SSO_LOOKUP_TOOL` (default `true`). Always falls back to
  the ComCare Hotline (1800-222-0000) when the match is only approximate or
  not found.


## Architecture

Orchestrated by [Pipecat](https://github.com/pipecat-ai/pipecat), using its
browser-based WebRTC transport for interactive testing — no bespoke front-end
required.

```
transport.input()
    ↓
stt (MERaLiONSpeechTranslationService)      Hokkien audio → English text
    ↓
user_aggregator (LLMUserAggregator)         Collects transcribed text into a full user turn
    ↓
pre_llm_tagger (UserTurnPreLLMTagger)       Runs hybrid retrieval over knowledge_base/ and
    ↓                                       injects a <retrieved_evidence> block, per turn
llm (OpenAILLMService → OpenRouter gpt-oss-120b)   Grounded English answer
    ↓
chinese_renderer (ChineseRenderer)          Buffers the complete answer, renders it as
    ↓                                       Singapore Chinese via MERaLiON-3-10B
tts (OpenRouterTTSService)                   Text-to-speech (see Status above)
    ↓
transport.output()
    ↓
assistant_aggregator (LLMAssistantAggregator)
```

| Stage | Role |
|---|---|
| **MERaLiONSpeechTranslationService** | Segmented STT-shaped service; buffers VAD-closed audio, POSTs it to the MERaLiON `/v1/audio/translations` endpoint, emits English text |
| **Silero VAD** | Detects end-of-turn from the audio stream to drive turn-taking |
| **User/Assistant Aggregators** | Collect transcribed/generated text into full conversation turns |

# Ka-Ki-Gong: Hokkien Voice Access to Singapore Senior Support Schemes

Ka-Ki-Gong ("speak for yourself" in Hokkien) is a voice assistant prototype that
helps Singapore Hokkien-speaking seniors discover and understand caregiving and
senior-support schemes. A spoken Hokkien question is translated to English,
answered using a curated, locally-retrieved snapshot of
[SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/) scheme pages, and spoken
back in Singapore Chinese through a cloud text-to-speech model.

This is an accessibility research prototype, not an official integration with
SupportGoWhere, LifeSG, GovTech, MSF, MOH, AIC, or any other government agency.
It does not confirm eligibility or submit applications. See
[STREAMLINED_PIPELINE_CONTEXT.md](STREAMLINED_PIPELINE_CONTEXT.md) for the full
design specification this implementation follows.

## Status

**Implemented and wired into `bots/bot.py`:**

- Hokkien (or other supported language) speech → English text, via the
  MERaLiON speech-translation API ([services/meralion_speech_translation.py](services/meralion_speech_translation.py))
- Local hybrid retrieval (dense + lexical) over 303 curated SupportGoWhere
  scheme records in [knowledge_base/](knowledge_base/), run deterministically
  before every turn ([retrieval/](retrieval/), [processors/retrieval_tool.py](processors/retrieval_tool.py))
- Grounded English answer generation via `openai/gpt-oss-120b` through
  OpenRouter, with retrieved evidence injected into the system prompt each turn
- MERaLiON-3-10B English → Singapore Chinese rendering, run once per complete
  buffered assistant turn before TTS
  ([services/meralion_chinese_render.py](services/meralion_chinese_render.py),
  [processors/chinese_renderer.py](processors/chinese_renderer.py),
  [prompt/english_to_singapore-chinese.md](prompt/english_to_singapore-chinese.md)).
  The verified English answer is still what's stored in conversation context;
  only the spoken output is rendered as Singapore Chinese. Toggle with
  `ENABLE_CHINESE_RENDERER` (default `true`; set to `false` to send the
  grounded English answer directly to TTS as before).
- Text-to-speech via OpenRouter's `qwen/qwen-audio-3.0-tts-flash`
  ([services/openrouter_tts.py](services/openrouter_tts.py)). Note: this
  model's system voices only cover Mandarin Chinese and English — there is no
  Hokkien/Minnan voice, so spoken output is Mandarin-pronounced Singapore
  Chinese, not Hokkien.

  ([processors/sso_tool.py](processors/sso_tool.py),
  [retrieval/sso_lookup.py](retrieval/sso_lookup.py)) that looks up the
  Social Service Office nearest an area the user names, from a transcribed
  MSF contact list
  ([knowledge_base/social_service_offices/](knowledge_base/social_service_offices/)).
  Toggle with `ENABLE_SSO_LOOKUP_TOOL` (default `true`). Always falls back to
  the ComCare Hotline (1800-222-0000) when the match is only approximate or

toolCallRounds.response:
Your summary is correct. To be precise about the pipeline: `embed_query()` → `SchemeIndex.search()` computes `hybrid_score = alpha*cosine + (1-alpha)*BM25_norm` per scheme → top-`k` (default 3) sorted by that score → `format_evidence_block()` → spliced into `<retrieved_evidence>` in the system prompt → LLM call.

## Your scenario exposes a real gap: retrieval is turn-scoped, not accumulated

Look at `_tag_latest_user_message_if_needed()` → `_update_retrieval_evidence(content)`: `content` is **only the current turn's raw text**, never combined with earlier turns. And `_update_retrieved_evidence_metadata()` does a regex **replace** (`count=1`) of the `<retrieved_evidence>` block, not an append.

So for your example:

| Turn | Query text used for search | Evidence in system prompt after this turn |
|---|---|---|
| 1 "need money" | `"need money"` | financial-support schemes |
| 2 "mental health issue" | `"mental health issue"` (turn 1's text is **not** included) | mental-health schemes — **financial evidence is gone** |
| 3 "homeless" | `"homeless"` (turns 1-2 not included) | housing/shelter schemes — **mental-health evidence is gone too** |

By turn 3, the LLM's `<retrieved_evidence>` only contains homelessness-related schemes. It has no fresh evidence for financial or mental-health needs anymore, even though the user described all three. (The raw sentences "I need money" / "I have a mental health issue" are still sitting in the conversation's message history — the LLM can still *see* the user said them — but there's no scheme evidence backing those needs once overwritten.)

This matters most for a scheme that specifically addresses the **combination** (e.g. an integrated homelessness + mental health + financial-assistance program) — that would never surface, because no single turn's isolated text is ever used as the query; the composite need is never formed into one query string.

def _prettify_category(slug: str) -> str:
    """'caregiving_support' -> 'Caregiving support', for a readable topic line."""
    return slug.replace("_", " ").capitalize()


def _with_topic_context(record: SchemeRecord) -> str:
    """Prepend folder categories + API domain tags to embedding_text.

    knowledge_base/<category>/ folder names and each scheme's own scraped
    ``domains`` field are topic signal that previously only lived in
    SchemeRecord metadata, unused by dense/lexical scoring. Baking them into
    the text that actually gets embedded and BM25-indexed lets a query like
    "caregiving" or "financial support" match on topic terms, not just on
    words appearing in the scheme's own prose.
    """
    lines = [f"Categories: {', '.join(_prettify_category(c) for c in record.categories)}"]
    if record.domains:
        lines.append(f"Domains: {', '.join(record.domains)}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n" + record.embedding_text

    "sections": {
      "About this support": "SPIN aims to empower single parents and lone caregivers to be resilient and self-reliant, and to help them attain increased capacity in caregiving/parenting, improve their social support, psychological well-being and increase their access to practical resources.\n\nServices include:\n\n- Needs assessment by social workers and co-creation of individualised care plans with single parents/lone caregivers to address identified needs.\n- Counselling for single parents and children who have been assessed to be in need for emotional and mental health support.\n- Befriending and peer support for single parents to build social support and trust amongst other parents and volunteers\n- Counselling, tuition and homework support for the children (aged 7 to 17) of the clients\n- Workshops and events to empower single parents with essential life and career skills\n- Practical support such as referrals to resource channels to support clients in meeting identified needs, disbursement of grocery vouchers and food items",
      "Who is this for?": "- Single parents or lone caregivers of children below 18 years old, and these children\n- No income criteria and no geographical boundaries",
      "How to apply?": "You may\n\n1. Approach any Family Service Centre (FSC) for referral, or\n2. Sign up online at https://crm.hcsa.org.sg/spin-member-application-form/ to fill up the online registration form, or\n3. Call or email the programme for assistance in signing up.",
      "What to expect?": "A social work associate will respond to the enquiry/referral within 3-5 working days and arrange for intake assessment. Thereafter, a social worker will be assigned to the parent, and trained befrienders will be matched to the parent. The programme is for a maximum period of 12 months. After the programme ends, the parent will be invited to join the Alumni Chapter to continue staying connected with a community and contribute to a supportive network of single-parent families."
    }

    "sections": {
      "About this support": "- The DACs' programme is designed to equip persons with disabilities with daily living skills and community living skills to maximise their independence.\n- The activities also aim to meaningfully occupy persons with disabilities with social and recreational activities.\n- Therapeutic and behavioural intervention services may be provided at some centres.\n- DACs also provide a form of respite for caregivers during the day.",
      "Who is this for?": "Applicants should be:\n\n- 18 years old and above*^#\n- Singapore citizens or Permanent Residents^^\n- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:\n  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment\n  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye\n  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear\n  - Intellectual disability\n  - Autism\n\nProof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)** completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.\n\n- Applicants should not be suffering from any untreated infectious disease.\n\n*Students of Government and community-funded SPED schools should be encouraged to remain in school until graduation. Parents of SPED graduands may approach their School to discuss the transition plans of the children prior to graduating from School.\n\n^Applicants who are below age 21 will need consent of parents or legal guardians for their application.\n\n#Applicants who are aged 21 and above with no mental capacity, will need the consent of the appointed deputy(s)/donee(s) on behalf of the applicant.\n\n^^For Permanent Residents, at least one immediate family member must be a Singapore Citizen. Immediate family members refer to spouses, parents, children or the applicant, including stepparents and stepchildren.\n\n**From 8 September 2025, the [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) is the standardised proof of disability required to verify an individual’s disability status when applying for selected MSF disability schemes and services and other selected Government schemes. Applicants can check if their disability status is already verified via their Touchpoints, SupportGoWhere, or call SG Enable at [1800-8585-885](tel:1800-8585-885)",
      "How to apply?": "- Please approach a social service professional from a touchpoint (e.g. Social Service Agency (SSA), hospitals etc.) for assistance in submitting a DAC application. If you are currently not receiving support from any social service or medical touchpoints, you may [approach SG Enable for assistance](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/information-and-referral-services).\n- Before meeting your Touchpoints, all applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If you do not have a verified disability status, the Touchpoint will guide you to the relevant registered healthcare professionals to assist with DVF.\n\n**Submission of applications to SG Enable by Social Service Professional (Online or Hardcopy)**\n\n**Step 1:**\n\nAll applicants should check if they have a verified disability status by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with their Singpass. If the applicant already has a verified disability status, a DVF is not required.\n\n**Step 2:**\n\nIf the applicant does not have a verified disability status or has a new disability condition which has not been verified previously, registered Touchpoint Assessor/Admin must submit a copy of the DVF completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional together with the AD application.\n\n**Step 3:**\n\nRegistered touchpoints’ Assessor/Admin may submit clients’ AD application and completed DVF online via CorpPass (recommended) or via hardcopy.\n\n1. **Online submission (Recommended)**\n  Log into e-Services using your CorpPass\n2. **Hardcopy submission**\n  Download the [AD application form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/ad-application-form.pdf?sfvrsn=71d5f444_3), print and send together with the required documents. If required, you may download sections of the AD application form and DVF below for use:\n  - [Client Assessment Form (Revised)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-caf-r-form.pdf?sfvrsn=c2d096c3_1)\n  - [Medical Information Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-interim-medical-information.pdf?sfvrsn=c4f804d4_1)\n  - [Declaration Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/declaration-form.pdf?sfvrsn=a7fa3568_2)\n  - [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)",
      "What to expect?": "- SG Enable will contact you within 10 working days upon receiving the completed application together with the required supporting documents from the touchpoint. SG Enable will also update the social worker who assisted in the application on the status of the application.\n- Acceptance into the programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies and approval of the centre management."

    "info_last_updated": "2026-06-30T03:53:47.423Z",
    "sections": {
      "About this support": "CTSP consists of the Caregivers-to-Caregivers (C2C) Programme and Engagement-to-Empowerment (E2E) Programme. C2C aims to provide caregivers with the knowledge and skills regarding caregiving so that they can better cope with their caregiving duties.\n\nC2C provides various types of training courses that range from 8 to 12 sessions and in 3 different languages, to cover general or specific mental health conditions. Through the C2C training courses, caregiver leaders are also identified and trained to volunteer as caregiver leaders to support other caregivers in subsequent C2C classes and /or outreach and advocacy work.\n\nE2E consists of the following components:\n\n- Caregiver-for-Caregiver (C4C) Support Programme: 12 support group sessions over a year, with the aim of increasing support networks for caregivers. The first six sessions will be held in-person and will aim to provide support and equip caregivers with coping skills. Subsequent sessions may be a mix of online or in-person sessions, including self-run activities by caregivers with support from Mindfull Community Limited staff, to gather fellow caregivers for social activities or a sharing session.\n- Train-the-Trainer (TTT): Caregivers who indicated interest to contribute and identified by staff as having potential are coached and trained as Volunteer Trainers and/or to support advocacy and outreach work through “Train-the-Trainer” modules so they can volunteer to support CAL’s programmes and activities.",
      "Who is this for?": "- Caregivers of Persons with Mental Health Issues (PMHIs).\n- This can range from spouses, partners, parents, siblings, grandchildren, friends, neighbours, etc of someone who is experiencing a mental health condition.",
      "How to apply?": "Register online through the [form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=mH6MQ8-ncE-ro_WXOpzXWwTicfzzzZ1Jqtl-rNfRemJUMEpJWUo4NFFQVjZMWDE4NEs3N1hPWTBHNiQlQCN0PWcu&route=shorturl).",
      "What to expect?": "After registration, interested participants will receive a call and email from Mindfull Community Limited to confirm their registration.[form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=mH6MQ8-ncE-ro_WXOpzXWwTicfzzzZ1Jqtl-rNfRemJUMEpJWUo4NFFQVjZMWDE4NEs3N1hPWTBHNiQlQCN0PWcu&route=shorturl)"
    }

    "title": "Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)",
    "description": "A legal document that allows you (the 'Donor') to appoint one or more trusted persons (the 'Donee') to  make decisions on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity. ",
    "url": "https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-LPA",
    "keywords": [
      "Advance Care Planning",
      "Fees payable"
    ],
    "domains": [

      "Retirement and legacy planning"

    "profiles": [

    ],
    "highlights": [],

      "SG",

    ],
    "min_age": 21,
    "max_age": 150,
    "cost": "PAID",
    "info_last_updated": "2026-06-26T06:35:54.608Z",
    "sections": {
      "About this support": "An LPA allows you to appoint trusted individuals to make decisions on (i) personal welfare and (ii) property and affairs, on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity.",
      "Who is this for?": "Donors must:\n\n- Be 21 years old and above\n- Have the mental capacity to make your own decisions\n- Not be an undischarged bankrupt if you wish to make an LPA for property and affairs matters\n\nDonees must:\n\n- Be 21 years old and above\n- Be your spouse or partner, family member or relative, friend, or a licensed trust company for property and affair matters only\n- Have the mental capacity to make their own decisions",
      "How to apply?": "You can:\n\n- [Apply online](https://opg-eservice.msf.gov.sg/) or\n- You may also [book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) or visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) today for in-person guidance and assistance\n  for your application. Please note that a [LPA certificate issuer](https://book.health.gov.sg/lpa) is required to ensure that the donor has the mental capacity to make a LPA.",
      "What to expect?": "Here are the steps on how to make an LPA:\n\n- Step 1: Decide on the type of LPA form\n  - LPA Form 1 grants general powers to Donee(s) who will make decisions on your behalf when you lose mental capacity\n  - LPA Form 2 is for applicants who want to appoint more than 2 Donees and/or more than 1 replacement Donee, and grant specific or customised powers that are not in the scope of LPA Form 1. You will need to engage a lawyer for LPA Form 2.\n- Step 2: [Find an LPA certificate issuer ](https://book.health.gov.sg/lpa)who is:\n  - A medical professional accredited by the OPG\n  - A registered psychiatrist\n  - A practising lawyer (excluding lawyers registered under section 36E of the Legal Profession Act 1966)\n- You and the LPA certificate issuer must digitally sign the LPA using the Singpass app. Your Donees can sign electronically by accepting their appointment.\n- For your LPA to be legally valid, the certificate issuer must submit the LPA application to Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) via OPG Online (OPGO), as authorised by you."
    }

    "highlights": [
      "Parents may nominate child to receive payouts from their CPF savings after they pass on",
      "Minimum monthly payout is $250, parents may decide on a higher amount",
      "Submit the application and supporting documents to SNTC via email or mail"
    ],
    "citizenship": null,
    "min_age": null,
    "max_age": null,
    "cost": null,
    "info_last_updated": "2026-06-16T08:05:50.133Z",
    "sections": {
      "About this support": "- Parents may nominate child with special needs to receive payouts from their CPF savings after death with minimum monthly payout of $250.\n- If the nominating parent’s CPF savings upon his/her demise is insufficient to support a year’s worth of payout (e.g. a minimum monthly payout is S$250 x 12 months = S$3,000), the CPF savings will be disbursed as a lump sum to the nominee with special needs.",
      "Who is this for?": "The nominating applicant should be:\n\n- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident\n- The parent or an appointed legal guardian of the child with special needs\n\nThe child with special needs should:\n\n- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:\n  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment\n  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye\n  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear\n  - Intellectual disability\n  - Autism\n\nProof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.\n\n**Or**\n\n- is attending or had attended a Special Education School\n\nThe 6 ADLs are:\n\n- Eating\n- Bathing\n- Dressing\n- Transferring\n- Toileting\n- Walking or moving around",
      "How to apply?": "Before proceeding, all applicants are encouraged to check if your child’s disability status has already been verified.\n\nFind out more here: https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification\n\nYou can apply by submitting the completed [application form](https://www.sgenable.sg/snss) and supporting documents:\n\n- via mail to Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), Future Care Planning Resource Centre by SG Enable, 22 Lengkok Bahru, Vista, Enabling Village #03-03  Singapore 159824\n- via email to [futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg).\n\nYou'll need to provide copies of:\n\n- Nominating applicant's and child's NRIC\n- Child's Birth Certificate\n\nIf your child's disability status has not been verified:\n\n- Supporting document from the SPED school issued on the school’s official letterhead stating that the Person with Special Needs (PSN) is currently attending or has previously attended the SPED school or\n- [Disability Verification Form (DVF) ](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)completed by a Registered Healthcare Professional*\n\nAfter mailing the application and upon approval by MSF, parents will receive an eligibility letter, which they should bring to the CPF Board to make the SNSS nomination.\n\n*Please note that a submitted Disability Verification Form (DVF) does not mean that your child’s disability status has been verified.",
      "Where to go": "[22 Lengkok Bahru 159824](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159824)\n\nFuture Care Planning Resource Centre by SG Enable,\n\nEnabling Village #03-03",
      "Agency website": "[View more details](https://www.sntc.org.sg/services/special-needs-savings-scheme-(snss))",
      "Email / Form": "[futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg)",
      "Phone number": "Special Needs Savings Scheme Hotline:\n\n[6278 9598](tel:62789598)\n\n(Operating hours: 9am-6pm on weekdays, closed on weekends and public holidays)"
    }

      "How to apply?": "Applications for EASE (Private) will be rolled out in phases (based on age of seniors in the household in 2026):\n\n**When to Apply**\n**Who Can Apply**\n**From 1 Apr 2026 onwards**\nHouseholds with seniors aged 80 and above\nHouseholds with seniors aged 60 and above who require assistance with at least one of the Activities of Daily Living (ADL)\n**From 1 Jul 2026 onwards**\nHouseholds with seniors aged 70 and above\n**From 1 Oct 2026 onwards**\nHouseholds with seniors aged 65 and above\n\nLetters and SMSes will be progressively sent to eligible households to apply for EASE (Private).\n\nYou can apply via BCA’s [EASE (Private) Portal](https://go.gov.sg/ease-private).\n\nSeniors aged 60 to 64 who requires assistance for one or more of the Activities of Daily Living (ADL) must submit a [Functional Assessment Report](https://www.aic.sg/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Functional-Assessment-Report.pdf) endorsed by a qualified assessor, such as a doctor, registered nurse or registered physiotherapist/occupational therapist.",

      "About this support": "To support ageing in place, you may apply for the following subsidies for seniors who live at home:\n\n- Subsidies of up to 90% for approved mobility and assistive devices (e.g. mobility aids such as walking/quad stick, wheelchair, geriatric chair, commodes, pressure relief mattress/cushions, hospital beds, spectacles, hearing aids, etc.)\n- Subsidies of up to 80% for approved home healthcare items (e.g. milk feeds, diapers, etc.)",
      "Who is this for?": "- 60 years old and above\n- Singapore Citizen or PR\n- Monthly household income per capita of less than or equal to $4,800 (or property annual value of $21,000 or below for households with no income)\n- Pass a [means-test](https://aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Seniors-Mobility-and-Enabling-Fund---Mobility-and-Assistive-Devices#faq) for Intermediate and Long-Term Care (ILTC) services\n- Seniors and persons with disabilities will be served under one scheme and agency throughout their lifetime\n- If the individual has tapped on Assistive Technology Fund (ATF)^ before the age of 60, they will continue to be served by ATF throughout their lifetime and not SMF\n- If the individual has not tapped on ATF subsidies before the age of 60, they would be served by SMF throughout their lifetime\n- Individuals can approach their care provider, e.g. hospitals, community care organisations, social service agencies, to enquire about their eligibility for the schemes\n- They may also approach the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) if they are not currently receiving support from any care provider\n\n^ATF provides subsidies for persons with disabilities (PWDs) to purchase the assistive technology devices to enable independent living\n\nAdditional criteria for assistive devices:\n\n- Assessed by a qualified assessor to require the device\n- Must not reside in a nursing home or sheltered home\n\nAdditional criteria for motorised devices:\n\n- Must not have a full-time caregiver or domestic worker\n- Unable to use a manual wheelchair independently\n- Assessed to be mentally and physically able to safely use the motorised device\n\nAdditional criteria for home healthcare items:\n\n- Must not be a current recipient of subsidies for the same items\n- Must be receiving Home Nursing, Home Medical, Home Palliative Care, or Day Hospice services",
      "How to apply?": "You can apply:\n\n- via the therapist or social worker at the hospital, day rehabilitation centre, or senior care centre from which your loved one is receiving care\n- online [using Singpass](https://for.sg/smf-application-using-singpass) or [without Singpass](https://for.sg/smf-application-not-using-singpass)\n- By mailing the [completed application form for assistive device or mobility device](http://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/SMF-Application-Form.pdf) and supporting documents to Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF), No. 7 Maxwell Road #04-01, MND Complex Annex B, Singapore 069111\n\nYou'll need to provide:\n\n- Copy of Applicant's NRIC (front and back) or a copy of the digital NRIC available on SingPass\n- For first time application for motorised device, doctor memo or [Need for Assessment form](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/Cerification-of-Medical-Need-Form.pdf) indicating need for motorised device must be submitted.\n- Copies of medical reports, if available\n- Copies of financial assistance documents, if available",
