    "cost": "FREE",
    "info_last_updated": "2026-04-30T02:35:49.493Z",
    "sections": {
      "About this support": "A CPF nomination allows you to decide:\n\n- Who will receive your CPF savings (your “nominee”)\n- The percentage of your CPF savings each nominee should receive\n- CPF savings **cannot be distributed by a will **as CPF savings do not form part of your estate. This arrangement **protects your CPF savings from creditor claims** on any outstanding debts you may have and preserves your savings fully for your nominees.\n\nYour CPF nomination will cover:\n\n- CPF savings in your Ordinary, Special, MediSave and Retirement Accounts\n- CPF LIFE premium balance\n- Your discounted Singtel shares (if any)\n\nYour CPF nomination does not cover:\n\n- Properties bought using your CPF savings\n- Payout from the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS)\n- Investments under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)",
      "Who is this for?": "To make a CPF nomination, you must:\n\n- Be a CPF member\n- Be aged 16 years and above\n- Have the mental capacity to make your own decisions\n\nYou can **nominate any person or legal entity*** to be the beneficiary of your CPF savings.\n\n*An entity that is capable of receiving monies in its own right.",
      "How to apply?": "You can:\n\n- Apply [online](http://cpf.gov.sg/MakeCPFNOM) using your Singpass\n- [Make an appointment](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form) to apply in person at any CPF service centre if you are unable to find two witnesses\n- [Book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) to visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) for in-person guidance on your online nomination application. Click [here](https://www.psd.gov.sg/servicesg/) for the list of ServiceSG Centres and their operating hours\n\n**For online application**\n\nYou will need to have:\n\n**Your nominees’ particulars**\n\n1. Full Name\n2. NRIC or Foreign Identification Number (FIN)\n3. Mailing Address (for foreigners)\n4. Email Address (optional)\n\n**Two witnesses’ particulars**\n\n1. Full Name\n2. NRIC\n3. Email address and/or Singapore-registered mobile phone number\n4. Cannot be a nominee\n5. He/she cannot be a nominee and must be at least 21 years of age\n\nUpon submission of your nomination,** inform your witnesses to log in **[here](http://cpf.gov.sg/witnessNOM)** within 7 calendar days to witness your nomination using their Singpass.**\n\n**For in-person application**\n\nYou will need to bring along and prepare:\n\n- A copy of your NRIC/passport\n- Your nominee(s)' NRIC number or Foreign Identification Number (FIN), email (optional), and mailing address (for foreigners)\n\nAs CPF Board's customer service executives or ServiceSG staff are acting as your witnesses, you do not need to prepare your witnesses' particulars.",
      "What to expect?": "If your nominee falls into the following categories, here is what to expect:\n\n**Below 18 Years Old**\nThe monies will be held in trust by the Public Trustee until your nominee turns 18.\n**Unable To Make Decisions Independently**\nThe monies will be handled by their court appointed deputy.\n**Bankrupt**\nThe monies belonging to the undischarged bankrupt nominee, will be transferred to the Official Assignee.\n\nTo allow your CPF savings to be distributed swiftly according to your wishes when you pass on, it is important to **review your CPF nomination regularly**, especially at key milestones (e.g.):\n\n- Starting Work\n- Marriage*\n- Childbirth\n- Divorce\n- Death of a nominee\n- When you reach your golden years**\n\n*Your nomination will be revoked upon marriage, and you should make a new nomination.\n\n**Review your nomination and consider your current family circumstances, such as which family member may need your savings more."
    }
  },

    "sections": {
      "About this support": "Advance Care Planning (ACP) is an ongoing process of planning and preparing for your future health and personal care. It includes conversations about your:\n\n- personal beliefs\n- values\n- healthcare preferences\n\nThese will be shared with your loved ones and healthcare team.\n\nHaving a quality ACP ensures that this process is person-centred, informed and guided. In the event that you lose the capacity to make decisions or speak for yourself, the ACP will help your loved ones and healthcare team act in your best interests based on your prior expressed wishes.",
      "Who is this for?": "- For any individuals aged 21 years old* and above who has the capacity to make their own decisions.\n- Includes people who are healthy and living with chronic or any other medical conditions.\n\nACP is particularly important for people who are living with a health condition. You can consult your regular doctor, especially if you have chronic conditions (e.g. diabetes, heart disease, chronic kidney disease) or any other medical concerns.\n\n*For individuals below 21 years old and living with a health condition, please approach your healthcare team if you are interested to find out more about ACP.",
      "How to apply?": "You can:\n\n1. Use the [myACP online service](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/acp/)\n\nComplete your ACP without having to speak to an ACP facilitator. You can use the [myACP online service](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/acp/) if you:\n\n- have a Singpass account\n- are at least 21 years old\n- do not have any existing serious illness\n- do not have a Preferred Plan of Care (PPC) ACP or Disease Specific (DS) ACP\n\nOnce you’ve completed the online form, your NHS will receive digital invitations. They’ll be notified via SMS, and must accept or reject their appointment by logging in to My Legacy with their Singpass. Your ACP will automatically be registered once all your NHS have accepted their appointments.\n\n1. Book an appointment with an ACP facilitator\n\n[Visit an ACP service provider](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/listing/acp-providers/results) if you:\n\n- prefer to have a conversation with an ACP facilitator and be guided\n- have an existing serious illness*\n\nYour ACP will be registered in the National Electronic Health Records (NEHR) upon completing all discussions with your facilitator. Some service providers may charge a nominal fee. Please check with the respective organisation for details.\n\n* Serious illnesses include: Cancer, Stroke, End Stage Renal Failure (ESRF), Severe Liver Disease, Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), Congestive Heart Failure (CHF), Dementia, and Chronic Neurological Disease.\n\n1. [Book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) or visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) today for in-person guidance and assistance for your application.\n\nYou may also refer to [this website](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/end-of-life-planning/advance-care-planning/) for more information on steps to prepare your ACP.",
      "What to expect?": "- You will need to appoint a Nominated Healthcare Spokesperson (NHS) who is responsible for speaking on your behalf about your healthcare preferences when you are no longer able to do so. In such situations, the healthcare team will consult your NHS and discuss your care plan.\n- After completing your ACP, it will be available on the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR), where your healthcare team can access and refer to your ACP to prepare your care plan."
    }
  },

      "About this support": "- The Government will match every dollar of cash top-ups made to the MA of eligible beneficiaries, up to $1,000 per year, starting from January 2026, for a period of five years\n\n- The matching grant will automatically be credited to the MA of the eligible member at the beginning of the following year, i.e. from 2027\n\n- Eligible beneficiaries will enjoy interest rates of up to 6% per annum on the cash top-ups and matching grant\n\n- Cash top-ups that attract the Matched MediSave Scheme matching grant will not qualify for tax relief",
      "Who is this for?": "- Singapore Citizen\n- Between 55 and 70 (inclusive) as of 31 December of the year\n- Does not own more than 1 property\n- Annual Value of residence not more than $21,000\n- Average monthly income not more than $4,000\n- MA balance less than half the current Basic Healthcare Sum",
      "How to apply?": "- No application is required\n- Eligibility is automatically assessed annually at the beginning of the year, starting from January 2026\n  - If you are eligible, CPF Board will notify you via email or post\n  - To receive the matching grant, you need to [receive cash top-ups in your MA](http://www.cpf.gov.sg/topupmedisave) within the year that you are eligible for Matched MediSave Scheme",
      "Where to go": "[Visit your nearest branch](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/contact-us/visit-us)\n\nNote: Please [book an appointment](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form) before making a visit.",

      "About this support": "- Subsidy of up to 90% of the cost of the required assistive technology device (lifetime cap of $40,000)\n- Subsidy amount is determined according to the applicant's monthly household income\n- Funds can be used to buy, replace, upgrade, or repair assistive technology devices\n- The Fund does not support consumables. The Fund will cover medical devices (e.g. oxygen concentrators and suction pumps) and spectacles for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents at or above age 60, who remain served by ATF.",
      "Who is this for?": "- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents\n- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:\n  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment\n  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye\n  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear\n  - Intellectual disability\n  - Autism\n\nProof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.\n\nUndergone qualified assessor’s assessment to determine the need and type of device(s)\n\n- Monthly Per Capita Household Income of $4,800 and below\n- Annual Value (AV) of residence reflected on NRIC of $21,000 and below for households with no income\n\n**Note for Singaporean and Permanent Resident Seniors:**\n\nSubject to eligibility,\n\n(a) Singaporean and Permanent Resident seniors who have not tapped on ATF before the age of 60 will be supported by the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF). Please apply to SMF.\n\n(b) Singaporean and Permanent Resident seniors who have tapped on ATF before the age of 60 will be supported by ATF throughout their lifetime.",
      "How to apply?": "- Approach a therapist or a social worker from public hospitals or social service agencies to assess and assist you to submit the application\n  - If you are not currently under the care of any public hospitals or social service agencies, you may approach a polyclinic to obtain a referral letter to a public hospital for an assessment and thereafter submit the application.\n- Before meeting your touchpoints, all applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If you do not have a verified disability status, the touchpoint's registered healthcare professional will be able to guide you with the disability verification.\n- Means testing is required and this will be assisted by the social worker at the public hospitals or social service agencies.",
      "Where to go": "[Enabling Village](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)\n[20 Lengkok Bahru ](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)\n[#01-01, Singapore 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)",
      "Agency website": "[View more details](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/assistive-technology/assistive-technology-fund)",
      "Email / Form": "[contactus@sgenable.sg](mailto:contactus@sgenable.sg)",

    "description": "Enables executors or administrators to settle the deceased's taxes and outstanding debts using the estate's funds before distribution to beneficiaries. ",
    "url": "https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/P3m8eAvW",

    "citizenship": null,
    "min_age": null,

    "cost": null,
    "info_last_updated": "2025-12-08T02:30:00.999Z",
    "sections": {
      "About this support": "Executors or administrators of a deceased can act on the deceased’s following matters:\n\n- Filing personal income tax for the deceased on the income earned up to the date of death.\n- Filing estate or trust income tax for the deceased on the income. Estate income refers to the income generated by the deceased’s assets after date of death, during the administration of the estate. Trust income refers to the income from assets held in trust.\n- Settling the taxes and other bills such as loans, funeral expenses and medical bills from the estate funds of the deceased before distribution to deceased’s beneficiaries.",
      "Who is this for?": "- Executors or administrators of a deceased’s estate who are responsible for settling outstanding taxes, debts and liabilities.\n- Remember, the executor or administrator must ensure all outstanding taxes, loans, funeral expenses, and medical bills are paid from the deceased's estate before distributing the remaining assets to the beneficiaries.",
      "How to apply?": "File personal income tax for the deceased\nProvide IRAS with the following details via [myTaxMail](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/portal/correspondence/mytax-mail):\n- Name, address and identification number of the legal personal representative who is handling the affairs of the deceased;\n- Copy of the death certificate;\n- Copy of the Grant of Probate/Letter of Administration, if available;\n- Income details from all sources, up to the date of death (please specify the breakdown for each income source); and\n- Type and amount of tax relief available/applicable to reduce the tax burden.\nFile an Income Tax Return for Estate or Trust Income\n- Download and complete the Request Form for Form T from [IRAS's website](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/other-taxes/trusts/filing-estate-trust-income-tax-(form-t)/form-t).\n- Email the completed form to [trust@iras.gov.sg ](mailto:trust@iras.gov.sg)and IRAS will provide you with:\n  - a Trust Reference Number\n  - a copy of Form T to complete\n- Mail the completed Form T to this address: The Comptroller of Income Tax, 55 Newton Road, Singapore 307987.",
      "Where to go": "55 Newton Road, Revenue House, Singapore 307987",
      "Agency website": "[View more details ](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/my-situation/my-family-member-has-passed-away)",
      "Email / Form": "[Submit an enquiry](https://www.iras.gov.sg/contact-us)",
      "Phone number": "For guidance, consult a lawyer or contact IRAS directly at [1800 356 8300](tel:1800-356-8300) or visit the IRAS office at 55 Newton Road, Revenue House, Singapore 307987, from Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm.  \n\nIf you need to speak with a tax officer, you are encouraged to [make an appointment](https://eappointment.iras.gov.sg/eappt/) at least 2 working days in advance."
    }
  },

    "type": "scheme",
    "title": "Pioneer Generation Package ",
    "description": "Special recognition to our Pioneer Generation through a package that assures them of affordable healthcare.  ",

    "citizenship": null,

    "max_age": null,
    "cost": null,
    "info_last_updated": "2025-10-03T07:07:37.877Z",
    "sections": {
      "About this support": "Provides the following benefits to support healthcare for Pioneers:\n\nMediSave Top-Ups\n- Annual MediSave top-ups for life, ranging from $300 to $1,200 depending on birth cohort, to offset premiums for MediShield Life, ElderShield and CareShield Life.\n- Additional MediSave top-ups of $50 to $200 will be disbursed from 2021 to 2025 for older Pioneers (i.e. those aged 82 and above in 2021) with serious pre-existing conditions who are paying additional premiums.\nAdditional Outpatient Care Subsidies\n- Additional subsidies for outpatient care at polyclinics, public Specialist Outpatient Clinics and Community Health Assist Scheme clinics.\nSpecial MediShield Life Premium Subsidies\n- Supports Pioneers in paying their MediShield Life premiums with special premium subsidies of up to 60%.\n- Combined with the MediSave top-ups ($300 - $1,200), Pioneers born in 1934 or earlier will see their MediShield Life premiums fully covered, and Pioneers born from 1935 to 1949 will have about two-thirds of their MediShield Life premiums covered.\nPioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme\n- Grants life-long cash assistance of $100 each month for those needing permanent assistance with at least 3 out of 6 of the following Activities of Daily Living:\n  - Eating\n  - Bathing\n  - Dressing\n  - Transferring\n  - Toileting\n  - Walking or moving around\n[Incentives have ceased]\nCareShield Life Additional Participation Incentives\n- Provides participation incentives (totalling $3,000) to encourage Pioneers to join CareShield Life by 31 Dec 2024, in addition to any other premium subsidies seniors may receive.\n\nIf you would like [more details on the above benefits as well as other useful information about this Package, please refer here.](https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/pioneer-generation-package)",
      "Who is this for?": "- Singapore Citizen\n- Born on or before 31 December 1949 and acquired citizenship on or before 31 December 1986\n- Eligible applicants have been notified in 2014\n- You may check your eligibility by:\n  - Using the LifeSG app to view your Pioneer Generation e-card; or\n  - Logging in to the Singpass mobile app to view your eligibility status",
      "How to apply?": "- No application required\n- Eligible individuals will receive the benefits automatically\n- To apply for the Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme (PioneerDAS), visit [this site](https://www.aic.sg/financial-assistance/pioneer-generation-disability-assistance-scheme/) for more information",
      "Agency website": "[View more details](https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/pioneer-generation-package)",
      "Email / Form": "[Submit an enquiry](mailto:contactus@pioneers.gov.sg)",
      "Phone number": "For general enquiries on Pioneer Generation eligibility, MediSave top-up, and MediShield Life Subsidy: [1800-222-2888](tel:1800-222-2888)\n\nFor loss of Pioneer Generation Card, and other healthcare-related enquiries: [1800-650-6060](tel:1800-650-6060)"
    }

edits.text:
topic tags to embedding_text.

    Prefers the scheme's own scraped ``domains`` (e.g. "Financial support and
    benefits") since it's finer-grained than, and a near-superset of, the
    knowledge_base/<category>/ folder names it was scraped into — falls back
    to prettified folder categories only if a scheme has no domains at all.
    Baking this into the text that actually gets embedded and BM25-indexed
    lets a query like "caregiving" or "financial support" match on topic
    terms, not just on words appearing in the scheme's own prose.
    """
    if record.domains:
        topic_line = f"Domains: {', '.join(record.domains)}"
    else:
        topic_line = f"Categories: {', '.join(_prettify_category(c) for c in record.categories)}"
    return topic_line

In `_update_retrieval_evidence()` in [bots/bot.py](bots/bot.py), there are two distinct "nothing to show" messages, and they mean different things:

|---|---|

| `"Retrieval was unavailable for this turn."` | The `try` block raised an exception — `embed_client.embed_query()` or `scheme_index.search()` threw — caught by `except Exception as exc:` |

Your log shows the second one, so something in the embed/search call itself failed for that turn — not a scoring/threshold miss.

`RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE` (default **0.0** per `env.example_cpp`) is the floor on `hybrid_score = alpha*cosine + (1-alpha)*BM25_norm` in `SchemeIndex.search()`. At `0.0`, virtually nothing gets filtered out by score alone (hybrid scores are rarely negative), so a threshold miss producing zero results would be unusual with default settings — that's more evidence this was a real error, not a low-relevance query.

- On other transient errors (timeouts, connection errors), uses exponential backoff (0.5s, 1s, capped at 5s).

This should let a turn survive a brief rate-limit blip instead of falling straight to "Retrieval was unavailable for this turn." If 429s persist frequently, it likely means you're exceeding OpenRouter's free-tier rate limit for that model — worth checking your OpenRouter dashboard for the actual limit, or switching to a paid/non-free embedding model if this happens often during normal conversation pacing.

## What this means for your case

`nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b:free` is a `:free` model, so it's subject to **both**:

#

# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD 2-Clause License

"""Build the local hybrid retrieval index from ``knowledge_base/``.

Embeds one complete Markdown page per scheme (not chunked — see
STREAMLINED_PIPELINE_CONTEXT.md section 3.3) via OpenRouter's
``nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b:free`` embedding model, then saves the result to
``data/`` for the bot to load at startup without needing network access.

Usage::

    uv run scripts/build_index.py

Reruns are cheap: this script always re-embeds every scheme from scratch, since
the corpus is small (a few hundred schemes) and OpenRouter's ``:free`` model
tier has no cost.
"""

import asyncio
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from loguru import logger

_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(_PROJECT_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_PROJECT_ROOT))

from retrieval.embeddings import OpenRouterEmbeddingClient  # noqa: E402
from retrieval.index import SchemeIndex  # noqa: E402

load_dotenv(dotenv_path=_PROJECT_ROOT / ".env", override=True)


async def main() -> None:
    kb_dir = _PROJECT_ROOT / os.getenv("KNOWLEDGE_BASE_DIR", "knowledge_base")
    data_dir = _PROJECT_ROOT / os.getenv("RETRIEVAL_DATA_DIR", "data")

    api_key = os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"]
    base_url = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_BASE_URL", "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1")
    model = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_EMBEDDING_MODEL", "nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b:free")
    query_prefix = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_EMBED_QUERY_PREFIX", "")
    passage_prefix = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_EMBED_PASSAGE_PREFIX", "")

    if (data_dir / "embeddings.npy").exists():
        logger.warning(
            "Existing embeddings found at {} — they will be overwritten.",
            data_dir / "embeddings.npy",
        )

    logger.info("Building retrieval index from {} using {}", kb_dir, model)

    embed_client = OpenRouterEmbeddingClient(
        api_key=api_key,
        base_url=base_url,
        model=model,
        query_prefix=query_prefix,
        passage_prefix=passage_prefix,
    )
    try:
        index = await SchemeIndex.build(kb_dir, embed_client)
    finally:
        await embed_client.aclose()

    index.save(data_dir)
    logger.info(
        "Saved {} scheme embeddings (dim={}) to {}",
        index.scheme_count,
        index.manifest.get("dim"),
        data_dir,
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

That's OpenRouter's cheapest widely-used paid embedding model (per their own docs example), not subject to the `:free` tier's 20/min + 50-or-1000/day caps — regular per-account rate limits apply instead, and cost is tiny for embeddings (a few cents per million tokens). `qwen/qwen3-embedding-0.6b` is another inexpensive non-free option if you want to compare quality/cost.

**Important**: switching models changes the embedding dimension, so you must fully rebuild the index — it's not optional here:

```bash
uv run scripts/build_index.py
```

This re-embeds all 303 schemes under the new model and overwrites `data/embeddings.npy`/`data/schemes.json`/`data/manifest.json` (the manifest records `embedding_model`, so `bot.py`'s `SchemeIndex.load()` will reflect the new model on next startup). Then restart the bot.

One thing to double check: `bots/bot.py` also uses `OPENROUTER_EMBEDDING_MODEL` for live per-turn query embeddings (`embed_client`), so this single env var switches both the offline index-build step and the live bot consistently — you don't need to change anything else.

## What are embeddings?

Embeddings transform text into high-dimensional vectors where semantically similar texts are positioned closer together in vector space. For example, "cat" and "kitten" would have similar embeddings, while "cat" and "airplane" would be far apart.

These vector representations enable machines to understand relationships between pieces of text, making them essential for many AI applications.

...

# Embeddings
...
## Common use cases

Embeddings are used in a wide variety of applications:

**RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)**: Build RAG systems that retrieve relevant context from a knowledge base before generating answers. Embeddings help find the most relevant documents to include in the LLM's context.

**Semantic Search**: Convert documents and queries into embeddings, then find the most relevant documents by comparing vector similarity. This provides more accurate results than traditional keyword matching because it understands meaning rather than just matching words.

**Recommendation Systems**: Generate embeddings for items (products, articles, movies) and user preferences to recommend similar items. By comparing embedding vectors, you can find items that are semantically related even if they don't share obvious keywords.

**Clustering and Classification**: Group similar documents together or classify text into categories by analyzing embedding patterns. Documents with similar embeddings likely belong to the same topic or category.

**Duplicate Detection**: Identify duplicate or near-duplicate content by comparing embedding similarity. This works even when text is paraphrased or reworded.

# Embeddings

## Best practices

**Choose the right model**: Different embedding models have different strengths. Smaller models (like qwen/qwen3-embedding-0.6b or openai/text-embedding-3-small) are faster and cheaper, while larger models (like openai/text-embedding-3-large) provide better quality. Test multiple models to find the best fit for your use case.

**Batch your requests**: When processing multiple texts, send them in a single request rather than making individual API calls. This reduces latency and costs.

**Cache embeddings**: Embeddings for the same text are deterministic (they don't change). Store embeddings in a database or vector store to avoid regenerating them repeatedly.

**Normalize for comparison**: When comparing embeddings, use cosine similarity rather than Euclidean distance. Cosine similarity is scale-invariant and works better for high-dimensional vectors.

**Consider Context Length**: Each model has a maximum input length (context window). Longer texts may need to be chunked or truncated. Check the model's specifications before processing long documents.
...

**Use Appropriate Chunking**: For long documents, split them into meaningful chunks (paragraphs, sections) rather than arbitrary character limits. This preserves semantic coherence.

## Provider routing

You can control which providers serve your embedding requests using the `provider` parameter. This is useful for:

* Ensuring data privacy with specific providers
* Optimizing for cost or latency
* Using provider-specific features

Example with provider preferences:

```typescript lines theme={null}
{
  "model": "openai/text-embedding-3-small",
  "input": "Your text here",
  "provider": {
    "order": ["openai", "azure"],
    "allow_fallbacks": true,
    "data_collection": "deny"
  }
}
```

For more information, see [Provider Routing](/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection).

## Error handling

Common errors you may encounter:

**400 Bad Request**: Invalid input format or missing required parameters. Check that your `input` and `model` parameters are correctly formatted.

**401 Unauthorized**: Invalid or missing API key. Verify your API key is correct and included in the Authorization header.

**402 Payment Required**: Insufficient credits. Add credits to your OpenRouter account.

**404 Not Found**: The specified model doesn't exist or isn't available for embeddings. Check the model name and verify it's an embedding model.

**429 Too Many Requests**: Rate limit exceeded. Implement exponential backoff and retry logic.

**529 Provider Overloaded**: The provider is temporarily overloaded. Enable `allow_fallbacks: true` to automatically use backup providers.

## Limitations

* **No Streaming**: Unlike chat completions, embeddings are returned as complete responses. Streaming is not supported.
* **Token Limits**: Each model has a maximum input length. Texts exceeding this limit will be truncated or rejected.
* **Deterministic Output**: Embeddings for the same input text will always be identical (no temperature or randomness).
* **Language Support**: Some models are optimized for specific languages. Check model documentation for language capabilities.

Don't use the `:batch` variant here — it's not just a pricing/rate-limit tier suffix, it's a **completely different, asynchronous API**.

## What `:batch` actually means on OpenRouter

Per their [Batch API docs](https://openrouter.ai/docs/batch-quickstart.md), batch requests go through a separate endpoint (`POST https://openrouter.ai/api/beta/batches`), not the regular `POST /embeddings` your code calls. Key differences:

- You submit a whole array of requests at once and get back `202 Accepted` with `status: "validating"` — no embeddings in the response.
- Results aren't ready until you poll `GET /api/beta/batches/:id` and the status reaches `completed` — the **completion window is 24 hours**. It's explicitly "for work that doesn't need an immediate response."
- It's ~50% cheaper than sync pricing, but that's the tradeoff for not getting an immediate answer.

## Why it doesn't fit either of your two embedding call sites

1. **Live per-turn query embedding** ( → ): needs the vector back within the same conversation turn. Waiting up to 24h is a non-starter for a voice bot.
2. **Offline index build** (): technically tolerant of delay, but it would require rewriting  to submit a batch job, poll for completion, and parse the very different `results[].response.body` shape — real engineering effort for a one-time job that already completes in seconds via the sync endpoint.

## What to use instead

Stick with the plain model ID, no suffix:

Don't use the `:batch` variant here — it's not just a pricing/rate-limit tier suffix, it's a **completely different, asynchronous API**.

## What `:batch` actually means on OpenRouter

Per their [Batch API docs](https://openrouter.ai/docs/batch-quickstart.md), batch requests go through a separate endpoint (`POST https://openrouter.ai/api/beta/batches`), not the regular `POST /embeddings` your code calls. Key differences:

- You submit a whole array of requests at once and get back `202 Accepted` with `status: "validating"` — no embeddings in the response.
- Results aren't ready until you poll `GET /api/beta/batches/:id` and the status reaches `completed` — the **completion window is 24 hours**. It's explicitly "for work that doesn't need an immediate response."
- It's ~50% cheaper than sync pricing, but that's the tradeoff for not getting an immediate answer.

## Why it doesn't fit either of your two embedding call sites

1. **Live per-turn query embedding** (`bots/bot.py` → `embed_client.embed_query()`): needs the vector back within the same conversation turn. Waiting up to 24h is a non-starter for a voice bot.
2. **Offline index build** (`scripts/build_index.py`): technically tolerant of delay, but it would require rewriting `OpenRouterEmbeddingClient` to submit a batch job, poll for completion, and parse the very different `results[].response.body` shape — real engineering effort for a one-time job that already completes in seconds via the sync endpoint.

## What to use instead

Stick with the plain model ID, no suffix:
```ini
OPENROUTER_EMBEDDING_MODEL=openai/text-embedding-3-small
```
This uses the normal synchronous `/embeddings` endpoint your existing `OpenRouterEmbeddingClient` already calls — no code changes needed beyond the env var, as I described earlier. Then rerun `uv run scripts/build_index.py` and restart the bot.

# Batch API Quickstart
...
## Limitations

The Batch API is currently text-only. On `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and `/v1/messages`, validation rejects any request that carries image, audio, video, or file content parts. That includes the Responses `input_image` and `input_file` parts and the Anthropic `image` and `document` blocks. On `/v1/chat/completions`, validation also rejects requests that ask for non-text output through `modalities`, `audio`, or `image_config`. For embeddings, `input` must be strings or token arrays.

Send multimodal requests to the sync API instead.

***

...

...
# Batch API Quickstart
...
## Pricing

Batch requests are typically billed at 50% of the model's standard per-token pricing, mirroring the batch discounts offered by [OpenAI](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch) and [Anthropic](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/batch-processing). For a completed batch, `usage.cost` reports the amount OpenRouter charges. For BYOK-routed batches, that's only the OpenRouter BYOK fee, since the provider bills you directly for inference.

<Note>
  Non-token pricing components aren't uniformly discounted. Web-search calls bill at standard rates, and prompt-caching rates vary by model. The pricing shown on each model's page is the source of truth.
</Note>

***

...

...
# Batch API Quickstart
...
## BYOK

If you have a [provider key](/docs/guides/overview/auth/byok) configured, batches route through it automatically, the same as sync requests: the provider bills you directly for inference and OpenRouter charges only the BYOK fee (see Pricing above). Completed batches report `usage.is_byok: true`.

Google Vertex uses a bucket in your GCP project for provider input and output. The primary setup is frictionless: omit `bucket` and let OpenRouter create a private, location-compatible bucket on the first batch. You can optionally provide an existing bucket instead. See [Google Vertex API keys](/docs/guides/overview/auth/byok#google-vertex-api-keys) for permissions and storage behavior.

***

# Batch API Quickstart
...
## Submit a batch

Submit a batch with:

```text title="Endpoint" lines theme={null}
POST https://openrouter.ai/api/beta/batches
```

The request body has three required top-level fields:

| Field      | Description                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `endpoint` | The API shape used by every request in the batch. Choose `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, or `/v1/embeddings`.                  |
| `model`    | An OpenRouter model slug, such as `openai/gpt-4o`. This batch-level model is applied to every request.                                                  |
| `requests` | A non-empty array of `{ custom_id, body }` items. `custom_id` must be unique within the batch, and `body` follows the shape of the selected `endpoint`. |

<Warning>
...

...
# Batch API Quickstart
...
## Submit a batch
...
  Serialize `endpoint` and `model` before `requests` in the JSON body. The API stream-parses the request so it can accept very large `requests` arrays without buffering, and it returns a `400` if `requests` appears first. Every example on this page already uses this order.
</Warning>

The batch-level `model` applies to every request. A request body can omit `model` to inherit the batch-level value. If a request body sets its own `model`, it must match the batch-level `model` or the submission is rejected.

On Google models, every request in a batch must ask for the same `response_format`. Either all requests omit it, all use `json_object`, or all use `json_schema` with the same schema. Google's batch service derives one output schema for the whole batch, so requests that disagree fail there. Validation fails a mismatched batch and names the first request that conflicts, so send one batch per `response_format` and per schema.

## List your batches

List the batches in the workspace of the authenticating API key with:

```shell title="Shell" lines theme={null}
curl 'https://openrouter.ai/api/beta/batches?limit=2&status=completed&status=failed' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY"
```

Batches are scoped to the workspace, not the key: every API key in the same workspace sees the same list, including batches submitted with other keys. Batches are returned newest first. List items contain metadata only and always set `results` to `null`; retrieve an individual batch by ID when you need its results.

```json title="Batch list" lines theme={null}
{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "batch_9f2c1e",
      "object": "batch",
      "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions",
      "model": "openai/gpt-4o",
      "completion_window": "24h",
      "status": "completed",
...

v.value:
Don't use the `:batch` variant here — it's not just a pricing/rate-limit tier suffix, it's a **completely different, asynchronous API**.

## What `:batch` actually means on OpenRouter

Per their [Batch API docs](https://openrouter.ai/docs/batch-quickstart.md), batch requests go through a separate endpoint (`POST https://openrouter.ai/api/beta/batches`), not the regular `POST /embeddings` your code calls. Key differences:

- You submit a whole array of requests at once and get back `202 Accepted` with `status: "validating"` — no embeddings in the response.
- Results aren't ready until you poll `GET /api/beta/batches/:id` and the status reaches `completed` — the **completion window is 24 hours**. It's explicitly "for work that doesn't need an immediate response."
- It's ~50% cheaper than sync pricing, but that's the tradeoff for not getting an immediate answer.

## Why it doesn't fit either of your two embedding call sites

1. **Live per-turn query embedding** (

): needs the vector back within the same conversation turn. Waiting up to 24h is a non-starter for a voice bot.
2. **Offline index build** (
): technically tolerant of delay, but it would require rewriting

to submit a batch job, poll for completion, and parse the very different `results[].response.body` shape — real engineering effort for a one-time job that already completes in seconds via the sync endpoint.

## What to use instead

Stick with the plain model ID, no suffix:
```ini
OPENROUTER_EMBEDDING_MODEL=openai/text-embedding-3-small
```
This uses the normal synchronous `/embeddings` endpoint your existing
already calls — no code changes needed beyond the env var, as I described earlier. Then rerun `uv run scripts/build_index.py` and restart the bot.

Given the actual shape of this project — small fixed corpus (~303 schemes), hybrid dense+BM25 scoring, a `<retrieved_evidence>` block that never changes format, and grounded LLM answers over voice — here's what's actually worth measuring, and I've built a starter harness for it.

## Two distinct things to evaluate

1. **Retrieval quality** (did the right scheme(s) surface in the top-k?) — this is measurable **objectively** with standard IR metrics if you have a small labeled query set. This should be your primary, repeatable benchmark since it's cheap, deterministic, and directly tunes `RETRIEVAL_TOP_K`/`RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA`/`RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE`/embedding model choice.
2. **End-to-end answer quality** (did the LLM's spoken reply follow the 14 grounding rules — no false eligibility claims, right hotline, no URLs, etc.) — this is much harder to define ground truth for, so **LLM-as-judge fits better here**, scoring the final spoken-style answer against your own prompt's rules.

Trying to use LLM-as-judge for #1 (raw retrieval) is weaker than it sounds — a judge model has to guess "is this scheme relevant" without ever seeing the actual eligibility text, so it just re-does a worse version of what your embeddings already do. It's more useful as a *supplement* for queries you haven't hand-labeled yet, not a replacement for labeled Recall/MRR.

#

"""Evaluate local hybrid retrieval quality against a small hand-labeled query set.

Computes standard IR metrics (Recall@k, MRR) against a labeled eval set (default:
eval/retrieval_eval_set.json), so retrieval quality can be tracked as you tune
RETRIEVAL_TOP_K / RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA / RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE or swap the
embedding model. Also supports an opt-in LLM-as-judge pass that scores the
top-3 results' relevance for each query (useful as a supplementary signal, not
a substitute for the labeled Recall/MRR metrics above).

Usage::

    uv run scripts/evaluate_retrieval.py
    uv run scripts/evaluate_retrieval.py --alpha 0.5 --top-k 5
    uv run scripts/evaluate_retrieval.py --llm-judge
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from loguru import logger

_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(_PROJECT_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_PROJECT_ROOT))

from retrieval.embeddings import OpenRouterEmbeddingClient  # noqa: E402
from retrieval.index import SchemeIndex  # noqa: E402

load_dotenv(dotenv_path=_PROJECT_ROOT / ".env", override=True)

DEFAULT_EVAL_SET = _PROJECT_ROOT / "eval" / "retrieval_eval_set.json"
RECALL_KS = (1, 3, 5, 10)


def load_eval_set(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


async def judge_relevance_llm(
    *, api_key: str, base_url: str, model: str, query: str, candidates: list[tuple[str, str]]
) -> list[int]:
    """Ask an LLM to rate each candidate's relevance to ``query`` on a 0-2 scale.

    ``candidates`` is a list of (title, description) pairs, same order as
    retrieved. Returns one int per candidate (0=not relevant, 1=somewhat,
    2=highly relevant); entries that fail to parse are -1.
    """
    listing = "\n".join(f"{i + 1}. {title}: {desc}" for i, (title, desc) in enumerate(candidates))
    prompt = (
        "You are judging search relevance for a Singapore senior-support scheme "
        "retrieval system. Given the user's need and a numbered list of candidate "
        "schemes, rate each candidate's relevance to the need on this scale:\n"
        "0 = not relevant, 1 = somewhat relevant, 2 = highly relevant / directly answers the need.\n\n"
        f"User need: {query}\n\nCandidates:\n{listing}\n\n"
        "Respond with ONLY a JSON array of integers, one per candidate, in order. "
        "Example: [2, 0, 1]"
    )
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0) as client:
        response = await client.post(
            f"{base_url}/chat/completions",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
            json={
                "model": model,
                "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
                "temperature": 0,
            },
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        content = response.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].strip()

    try:
        # Models sometimes wrap the array in prose or a code fence; grab the
        # first '[' ... ']' span rather than requiring an exact-match response.
        start, end = content.index("["), content.rindex("]") + 1
        scores = json.loads(content[start:end])
        return [int(s) for s in scores]
    except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        logger.warning("Could not parse LLM-judge response, skipping: {}", content[:200])
        return [-1] * len(candidates)


async def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--eval-set", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_EVAL_SET)
    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=10, help="Max results fetched per query")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--alpha", type=float, default=None, help="Override RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA for this run"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--llm-judge",
        action="store_true",
        help="Also score top-3 relevance via LLM-as-judge (costs one chat completion per query)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    data_dir = _PROJECT_ROOT / os.getenv("RETRIEVAL_DATA_DIR", "data")
    api_key = os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"]
    base_url = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_BASE_URL", "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1")
    embedding_model = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_EMBEDDING_MODEL", "nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b:free")
    judge_model = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_MODEL", "openai/gpt-oss-120b")
    alpha = args.alpha if args.alpha is not None else float(os.getenv("RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA", "0.7"))

    index = SchemeIndex.load(data_dir)
    embed_client = OpenRouterEmbeddingClient(api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url, model=embedding_model)

    eval_items = load_eval_set(args.eval_set)
    logger.info("Loaded {} eval queries from {}", len(eval_items), args.eval_set)

    hits_at_k = {k: 0 for k in RECALL_KS}
    reciprocal_ranks: list[float] = []
    per_query_rows: list[dict] = []

    for item in eval_items:
        query = item["query"]
        expected = set(item.get("expected_scheme_ids", []))

        query_embedding = await embed_client.embed_query(query)
        results = index.search(query, query_embedding, top_k=args.top_k, alpha=alpha)
        retrieved_ids = [r.scheme.scheme_id for r in results]

        rank = next((i + 1 for i, sid in enumerate(retrieved_ids) if sid in expected), None)
        reciprocal_ranks.append(1.0 / rank if rank else 0.0)
        for k in RECALL_KS:
            if rank is not None and rank <= k:
                hits_at_k[k] += 1

        row = {
            "query": query,
            "expected": sorted(expected),
            "top_results": [
                (r.scheme.scheme_id, r.scheme.title, round(r.hybrid_score, 3)) for r in results[:5]
            ],
            "rank_of_first_match": rank,
        }

        if args.llm_judge:
            candidates = [(r.scheme.title, r.scheme.description) for r in results[:3]]
            row["llm_judge_scores"] = await judge_relevance_llm(
                api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url, model=judge_model, query=query, candidates=candidates
            )

        per_query_rows.append(row)

    await embed_client.aclose()

    n = len(eval_items)
    print(f"\n=== Retrieval evaluation ({n} queries, alpha={alpha}, top_k={args.top_k}) ===\n")
    for row in per_query_rows:
        status = "HIT" if row["rank_of_first_match"] else "MISS"
        print(f"[{status}] rank={row['rank_of_first_match']}  {row['query']}")
        for sid, title, score in row["top_results"]:
            marker = "*" if sid in row["expected"] else " "
            print(f"    {marker} {sid:20s} {score:.3f}  {title}")
        if args.llm_judge:
            print(f"    LLM-judge scores (top-3): {row['llm_judge_scores']}")
        print()

    print("--- Summary ---")
    for k in RECALL_KS:
        print(f"Recall@{k}: {hits_at_k[k] / n:.2%}")
    print(f"MRR: {sum(reciprocal_ranks) / n:.3f}")

    asyncio.run(main())

Given the actual shape of this project — small fixed corpus (~303 schemes), hybrid dense+BM25 scoring, a `<retrieved_evidence>` block that never changes format, and grounded LLM answers over voice — here's what's actually worth measuring, and I've built a starter harness for it.

## Two distinct things to evaluate

1. **Retrieval quality** (did the right scheme(s) surface in the top-k?) — this is measurable **objectively** with standard IR metrics if you have a small labeled query set. This should be your primary, repeatable benchmark since it's cheap, deterministic, and directly tunes `RETRIEVAL_TOP_K`/`RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA`/`RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE`/embedding model choice.
2. **End-to-end answer quality** (did the LLM's spoken reply follow the 14 grounding rules — no false eligibility claims, right hotline, no URLs, etc.) — this is much harder to define ground truth for, so **LLM-as-judge fits better here**, scoring the final spoken-style answer against your own prompt's rules.

Trying to use LLM-as-judge for #1 (raw retrieval) is weaker than it sounds — a judge model has to guess "is this scheme relevant" without ever seeing the actual eligibility text, so it just re-does a worse version of what your embeddings already do. It's more useful as a *supplement* for queries you haven't hand-labeled yet, not a replacement for labeled Recall/MRR.

## What I built

A small labeled golden set + a metrics-first eval script, with an opt-in LLM-judge mode for supplementary scoring:

{"content": "#
# Copyright (c) 2024-2026, Daily
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD 2-Clause License
#

"""Evaluate local hybrid retrieval quality against a small hand-labeled query set.

Computes standard IR metrics (Recall@k, MRR) against a labeled eval set (default:
eval/retrieval_eval_set.json), so retrieval quality can be tracked as you tune
RETRIEVAL_TOP_K / RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA / RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE or swap the
embedding model. Also supports an opt-in LLM-as-judge pass that scores the
top-3 results' relevance for each query (useful as a supplementary signal, not
a substitute for the labeled Recall/MRR metrics above).

Usage::

    uv run scripts/evaluate_retrieval.py
    uv run scripts/evaluate_retrieval.py --alpha 0.5 --top-k 5
    uv run scripts/evaluate_retrieval.py --llm-judge
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from loguru import logger

_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(_PROJECT_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_PROJECT_ROOT))

from retrieval.embeddings import OpenRouterEmbeddingClient  # noqa: E402
from retrieval.index import SchemeIndex  # noqa: E402

load_dotenv(dotenv_path=_PROJECT_ROOT / ".env", override=True)

DEFAULT_EVAL_SET = _PROJECT_ROOT / "eval" / "retrieval_eval_set.json"
RECALL_KS = (1, 3, 5, 10)


def load_eval_set(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


async def judge_relevance_llm(
    *, api_key: str, base_url: str, model: str, query: str, candidates: list[tuple[str, str]]
) -> list[int]:
    """Ask an LLM to rate each candidate's relevance to ``query`` on a 0-2 scale.

    ``candidates`` is a list of (title, description) pairs, same order as
    retrieved. Returns one int per candidate (0=not relevant, 1=somewhat,
    2=highly relevant); entries that fail to parse are -1.
    """
    listing = "\n".join(f"{i + 1}. {title}: {desc}" for i, (title, desc) in enumerate(candidates))
    prompt = (
        "You are judging search relevance for a Singapore senior-support scheme "
        "retrieval system. Given the user's need and a numbered list of candidate "
        "schemes, rate each candidate's relevance to the need on this scale:\n"
        "0 = not relevant, 1 = somewhat relevant, 2 = highly relevant / directly answers the need.\n\n"
        f"User need: {query}\n\nCandidates:\n{listing}\n\n"
        "Respond with ONLY a JSON array of integers, one per candidate, in order. "
        "Example: [2, 0, 1]"
    )
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0) as client:
        response = await client.post(
            f"{base_url}/chat/completions",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
            json={
                "model": model,
                "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
                "temperature": 0,
            },
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        content = response.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].strip()

    try:
        # Models sometimes wrap the array in prose or a code fence; grab the
        # first '[' ... ']' span rather than requiring an exact-match response.
        start, end = content.index("["), content.rindex("]") + 1
        scores = json.loads(content[start:end])
        return [int(s) for s in scores]
    except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        logger.warning("Could not parse LLM-judge response, skipping: {}", content[:200])
        return [-1] * len(candidates)


async def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--eval-set", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_EVAL_SET)
    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=10, help="Max results fetched per query")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--alpha", type=float, default=None, help="Override RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA for this run"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--llm-judge",
        action="store_true",
        help="Also score top-3 relevance via LLM-as-judge (costs one chat completion per query)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    data_dir = _PROJECT_ROOT / os.getenv("RETRIEVAL_DATA_DIR", "data")
    api_key = os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"]
    base_url = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_BASE_URL", "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1")
    embedding_model = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_EMBEDDING_MODEL", "nvidia/nemotron-3-embed-1b:free")
    judge_model = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_MODEL", "openai/gpt-oss-120b")
    alpha = args.alpha if args.alpha is not None else float(os.getenv("RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA", "0.7"))

    index = SchemeIndex.load(data_dir)
    embed_client = OpenRouterEmbeddingClient(api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url, model=embedding_model)

    eval_items = load_eval_set(args.eval_set)
    logger.info("Loaded {} eval queries from {}", len(eval_items), args.eval_set)

    hits_at_k = {k: 0 for k in RECALL_KS}
    reciprocal_ranks: list[float] = []
    per_query_rows: list[dict] = []

    for item in eval_items:
        query = item["query"]
        expected = set(item.get("expected_scheme_ids", []))

        query_embedding = await embed_client.embed_query(query)
        results = index.search(query, query_embedding, top_k=args.top_k, alpha=alpha)
        retrieved_ids = [r.scheme.scheme_id for r in results]

        rank = next((i + 1 for i, sid in enumerate(retrieved_ids) if sid in expected), None)
        reciprocal_ranks.append(1.0 / rank if rank else 0.0)
        for k in RECALL_KS:
            if rank is not None and rank <= k:
                hits_at_k[k] += 1

        row = {
            "query": query,
            "expected": sorted(expected),
            "top_results": [
                (r.scheme.scheme_id, r.scheme.title, round(r.hybrid_score, 3)) for r in results[:5]
            ],
            "rank_of_first_match": rank,
        }

        if args.llm_judge:
            candidates = [(r.scheme.title, r.scheme.description) for r in results[:3]]
            row["llm_judge_scores"] = await judge_relevance_llm(
                api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url, model=judge_model, query=query, candidates=candidates
            )

        per_query_rows.append(row)

    await embed_client.aclose()

    n = len(eval_items)
    print(f"\n=== Retrieval evaluation ({n} queries, alpha={alpha}, top_k={args.top_k}) ===\n")
    for row in per_query_rows:
        status = "HIT" if row["rank_of_first_match"] else "MISS"
        print(f"[{status}] rank={row['rank_of_first_match']}  {row['query']}")
        for sid, title, score in row["top_results"]:
            marker = "*" if sid in row["expected"] else " "
            print(f"    {marker} {sid:20s} {score:.3f}  {title}")
        if args.llm_judge:
            print(f"    LLM-judge scores (top-3): {row['llm_judge_scores']}")
        print()

    print("--- Summary ---")
    for k in RECALL_KS:
        print(f"Recall@{k}: {hits_at_k[k] / n:.2%}")
    print(f"MRR: {sum(reciprocal_ranks) / n:.3f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

These are two independent knobs that act at different stages of `SchemeIndex.search()`:

```python
hybrid_scores = alpha * dense_scores + (1 - alpha) * lexical_scores
...
if matches_category(record) and float(hybrid_scores[i]) >= min_score
```

## `RETRIEVAL_HYBRID_ALPHA=0.7` — a **weighting** ratio

Controls how the combined score is *computed*: what fraction comes from dense (embedding cosine similarity) vs lexical (BM25) matching.

$$\text{hybrid\_score} = 0.7 \times \text{dense\_cosine} + 0.3 \times \text{BM25}_{\text{norm}}$$

At `0.7`, semantic/embedding similarity dominates (70%), with keyword overlap contributing the remaining 30%. Every candidate scheme gets a hybrid_score computed this way — this setting never removes anything, it only changes *how* things get ranked.

## `RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE=0.5` — a **filter** threshold

Applied *after* the hybrid_score above is computed: any scheme whose hybrid_score falls below `0.5` is dropped entirely, before ranking/top-k selection. This is a hard floor — it can shrink or empty your result set regardless of alpha.

## Practical difference

- Change `alpha` → results are re-ordered/re-weighted, but (mostly) the same candidate pool.
- Change `min_score` → results can disappear outright, even a scheme that would've ranked #1 gets excluded if its score doesn't clear the bar.

**Heads-up**: you changed `RETRIEVAL_MIN_SCORE` from the documented default of `0.0` (in `env.example_cpp`) to `0.5`. That's a meaningfully strict floor — for L2-normalized embeddings, cosine similarity for a genuinely relevant query-scheme pair often lands well below 0.5 (BM25-normalized scores range 0-1 too, but sparse matches are common). At `alpha=0.7`, hitting hybrid_score ≥ 0.5 requires roughly dense_cosine ≥ ~0.5-0.6 on its own (if lexical contributes little), which can realistically cause **"No verified scheme evidence was found"** for turns that should have matched something. Worth running `uv run scripts/evaluate_retrieval.py --alpha 0.7` with and without this threshold (`--top-k` won't help here since min_score isn't exposed as a CLI flag yet — want me to add one so you can sweep it too?) to check how much recall you're losing at `0.5`.

toolCallRounds.response:
Yes, your interpretation is correct — with a couple of nuances worth knowing.

## What Recall@k actually measures here

For each of the 133 queries, the script fetches the top-10 candidates and finds the **rank of the first result whose `scheme_id` is in that query's `expected_scheme_ids`**. Recall@k = the fraction of queries where that first correct hit occurred at rank ≤ k.

So **Recall@1 = 67.67%** means: *if you only look at the #1 (top-ranked) result, it was one of the accepted correct answers for 67.67% of your 133 test queries.*

Your run's numbers, read the same way:
- **Recall@1 (67.7%)**: top result alone is right about 2 out of 3 times.
- **Recall@3 (86.5%)**: if you look at the top 3 results, the correct scheme shows up somewhere in there 86.5% of the time.
- **Recall@5 (93.2%)** and **Recall@10 (96.2%)**: diminishing returns — most of the remaining misses get "rescued" by rank 2-3, and only ~3.8% of queries (5 of 133) never surfaced the correct scheme even within the top 10 fetched.

## Two nuances to keep in mind

1. **"Correct" is generous for grouped queries.** ~16 of your 133 queries have multiple `expected_scheme_ids` (deliberately ambiguous ones, e.g. the CareShield/ElderShield cluster). For those, a hit at rank 1 only requires *any one* of the accepted schemes to be there — it's not checking whether *all* the ambiguous options were found, just whether the search wasn't completely off-topic.
2. **This is really "success/hit rate@k", not textbook Recall@k.** True IR "recall" would measure what fraction of *all* relevant documents were retrieved. Here, since we only care "did we find at least one acceptable scheme," it's the commonly-used simplification for single-answer-style eval (same idea, just worth knowing the label is a bit loose).

**MRR (0.785)** is a companion number to Recall@1: it averages $1/\text{rank}$ across all queries (0 if never found in top 10). An MRR of 0.785 roughly corresponds to the correct answer landing around rank ~1.27 on average — consistent with Recall@1 being high but not perfect, and the near-misses (rank 2) not being far off.

**The 5 true misses** (never appeared even at rank 10) worth investigating first: `SILVERSUPPORT`, `SKILLS-ADVISORY`, `SVC-MSCM`, `SVC-WP`, and the CareShield/premium-subsidy group query (rank 7, not a miss but weak) — these are your best candidates for retrieval quality issues (wording mismatch, embedding model limitations, or genuinely under-described schemes).

uv run python -c "
import json, re
from pathlib import Path

eval_items = json.loads(Path('eval/retrieval_eval_set.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
result = json.loads(Path('eval/results/retrieval_eval_20260906T075905Z.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
records = {r['scheme_id']: r for r in json.loads(Path('data/schemes.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))}

who_re = re.compile(r'## Who is this for\?\s*\n(.*?)(?=\n## |\Z)', re.DOTALL)

out = []
for eq, rq in zip(eval_items, result['per_query']):
    expected = set(eq['expected_scheme_ids'])
    candidates = [t for t in rq['top_results'] if t[0] not in expected]
    if not candidates:
        continue
    out.append(f'=== QUERY: {eq[\"query\"]}')
    out.append(f'    expected={sorted(expected)}')
    for sid, title, score in candidates:
        rec = records.get(sid)
        if not rec:
            out.append(f'  ? {sid} ({title}) -- NOT FOUND in data/schemes.json')
            continue
        who = ''
        m = who_re.search(rec.get('embedding_text',''))
        if m:
            who = m.group(1).strip().replace(chr(10), ' ')[:300]
        out.append(f'  - {sid} | {title} | score={score}')
        out.append(f'      desc: {rec.get(\"description\",\"\")[:200]}')
        out.append(f'      who: {who}')
    out.append('')

Path('eval/_audit_dump.txt').write_text(chr(10).join(out), encoding='utf-8')
print('wrote', len(out), 'lines')

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support, Financial support and benefits, Healthcare and well-being\n\n# Long-Term Care Subsidies\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/Sucth2ke*\n\nProvides means-tested subsidies for long-term care services by MOH-funded long-term care providers.\n\n## Highlights\n- For home and community long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%\n- For institutional long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%\n- Additional subsidies of up to 15% for Singapore Citizens born in or before 1969\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Keywords:** Budget 2025, Seniors, Subsidies\n\n## About this support\n**For home and community long-term care services (e.g. Day Care, Community Rehabilitation services, Home Nursing, Home Medical)**\n\n- Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%\n- Additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969\n\n**For institutional long-term care services (e.g. Nursing Home)**\n\n- Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%\n- Additional 5% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents\n- Monthly per capita household income (PCHI) of less than or equal to $4,800 (or property annual value (AV) of less than or equal to $21,000 for households with no income)\n- Receiving long-term care services from MOH-funded providers\n\n## How to apply?\nPersons who require long-term care services can approach their doctor at the hospital, polyclinic, or Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) for assistance in applying for admission to a subsidised long-term care service.\n\n## Where to go\n[Find nearest AIC Link](https://www.aic.sg/about-us/aic-link-locations/)\n\n## Agency website\n- [Non-residential long-term care services](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/subsidy-framework-for-non-residential-long-term-care-services)\n- [Residential long-term care services](https://www.moh.gov.sg/managing-expenses/schemes-and-subsidies/subsidies-for-residential-long-term-care-services)\n\n## Email / Form\n[Submit your enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg)\n\n## Phone number\nAIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060)",

both an in-person annual Health Plan check-in and viewing of Health Plan on HealthHub within the qualifying period of 1 July 2026 to 31 December 2029.\n- Special subsidies for Healthier SG screening tests and vaccinations (for eligible Singapore Citizens)\n- Healthier SG Chronic Tier subsidy at Healthier SG clinics for CHAS cardholders with high medication requirements (for selected chronic medications at prices comparable to polyclinic prices)\n- Full MediSave coverage for treatment of chronic conditions listed under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), up to the relevant apply?\n**Self-enrol via HealthHub**\n\nIf you are eligible, you will be invited via SMS to enrol in Healthier SG. Contact the MOH hotline at 6325 9220\n\n**Enrol with caregiver's assistance**\n\nYou can grant your caregiver/family member/loved one access to your HealthHub, so they can use their smartphone to help you enrol in Healthier SG.     "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support\n\n# Severe Disability Assessment (SDA)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SDA*\n\nProvides an assessment of your disability status conducted by a Ministry of Health (MOH)-accredited severe disability assessor.\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR\n**Keywords:** Caregiver support, PWDs\n\n## About this support\nSDA is required if you are:\n\n- Applying for the following long-term care severe disability financial assistance schemes administered by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC):\n  - CareShield Life\n  - ElderShield\n  - ElderFund\n  - Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE)\n  - MediSave Care\n- Applying for supplement schemes of CareShield Life and ElderShield administered by private insurers – Great Eastern, Income and SingLife\n- Undergoing a disability review to ascertain continued scheme eligibility\n- Undergoing an underwriting to enroll into selected schemes\n\n## Who is this for?\nAnyone who require an SDA to determine your ability to perform each of the 6 Activities of Daily Living, as certified by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor.\n\nThese 6 activities are:\n\n- Feeding\n- Dressing\n- Toileting\n- Washing\n- Walking or moving around\n- Transferring from bed to chair and vice versa\n\n## How to apply?\nTo find a severe disability assessors near you, you may visit the [AIC's website](https://aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) and search using a postal code, address, or your device's current location.\n\nIf a service provider listed informs you that they do not conduct SDA, please [reach out to AIC with their details](mailto:apply@aic.sg).\n\nFor further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060).\n\n- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.\n- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.\n\nYou can also visit the nearest [AIC Link](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)[ ](#_msocom_1)or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).\n\n## What to expect?\n- **Assessments are strictly by appointment only**. Please call ahead to make an appointment with the clinic or assessor before going to the clinic.\n- You will need to bring along relevant medical reports or discharge summaries related to your assessment when you go for your SDA appointment.\n- If your care recipient requires a mental capacity assessment to be completed to obtain certification for the purpose of applying for AIC schemes, please explicitly request for it when making the appointment. Do note that mental capacity assessments can only be completed by doctors.\n- A typical SDA will last about 45 minutes or longer.\n- SDA fees are as follows, if:\n  - You visit an assessor’s clinic: $100\n  - An assessor visits your house: $250\n- You will be reimbursed the assessment fee which you have paid if you are assessed to be severely disabled.\n- For CareShield Life claims, the assessment fee for the first disability assessment will be waived, regardless of whether you are assessed to be severely disabled, or whether the claim is successful.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Family, parenting and relationships\n\n# HCSA SPIN\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-HDSSPIII*\n\nSPIN supports single parents and lone caregivers through casework and counselling, social support network such as befriending, practical support and an online portal of information and resources.\n\n**Who it targets:** Families\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR\n**Keywords:** Free, Resources and Support\n\n## About this support\nSPIN aims to empower single parents and lone caregivers to be resilient and self-reliant, and to help them attain increased capacity in caregiving/parenting, improve their social support, psychological well-being and increase their access to practical resources.\n\nServices include:\n\n- Needs assessment by social workers and co-creation of individualised care plans with single parents/lone caregivers to address identified needs.\n- Counselling for single parents and children who have been assessed to be in need for emotional and mental health support.\n- Befriending and peer support for single parents to build social support and trust amongst other parents and volunteers\n- Counselling, tuition and homework support for the children (aged 7 to 17) of the clients\n- Workshops and events to empower single parents with essential life and career skills\n- Practical support such as referrals to resource channels to support clients in meeting identified needs, disbursement of grocery vouchers and food items\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Single parents or lone caregivers of children below 18 years old, and these children\n- No income criteria and no geographical boundaries\n\n## How to apply?\nYou may\n\n1. Approach any Family Service Centre (FSC) for referral, or\n2. Sign up online at https://crm.hcsa.org.sg/spin-member-application-form/ to fill up the online registration form, or\n3. Call or email the programme for assistance in signing up.\n\n## What to expect?\nA social work associate will respond to the enquiry/referral within 3-5 working days and arrange for intake assessment. Thereafter, a social worker will be assigned to the parent, and trained befrienders will be matched to the parent. The programme is for a maximum period of 12 months. After the programme ends, the parent will be invited to join the Alumni Chapter to continue staying connected with a community and contribute to a supportive network of single-parent families.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Healthcare and well-being\n\n# MediSave Care\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/MEDISAVE_CARE*\n\nAllows Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with severe disability to make monthly cash withdrawals from their and/or their spouse’s MediSave Account for long-term care.\n\n## Highlights\n- Withdraw up to $200 cash per month\n- Processing time will take between 6 to 8 weeks\n- Apply through AIC eServices for Financing Services (eFASS)\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities\n**Keywords:** Cash payouts, Long-term care, Severely disabled\n\n## About this support\n- Supports severely disabled Singapore Citizens or Permanent residents with monthly cash withdrawals to support long-term care needs\n- Withdraw up to $200 per month from care recipient’s and/or their spouse's MediSave account\n- [Withdrawal amounts are dependent on the care recipient and/or their spouse’s MediSave account balance](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/healthcare-financing/medisave-care-for-long-term-care-needs)\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident\n- Aged 30 and above\n- MediSave account balance of at least $5,000 for both the care recipient and their spouse\n- Assessed by an MOH-accredited assessor to be unable to perform at least 3 out of the following 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):\n  - Washing\n  - Dressing\n  - Feeding\n  - Toileting\n  - Walking or moving around\n  - Transferring\n\n## How to apply?\nYou can apply:\n\n- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)\n- Via assistance from the nursing home your loved one is staying in\n- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)\n\nYou will need to contact an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor for a Severe Disability Assessment (SDA) as part of the application. Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) for a list of assessors.\n\n## Where to go\n[Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/MediSave-Care)\n\n## Email / Form\n[Submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg)\n\n## Phone number\nAIC hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060)\n\nCalls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits\n\n# Migrant Domestic Worker Levy Concession\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/MDW_LEVY_CONCESSION*\n\nProvides concessionary levy at $60 per month if there is an eligible person residing in the household.\n\n## Highlights\n- Concessionary rate of $60 per month, compared to standard levy of $300 for 1st MDW and $450 for subsequent MDWs\n- Each household is eligible for one MDW levy concession per eligible person, up to two MDW levy concessions per household\n\n**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Keywords:** Caregiving expenses, Subsidies\n\n## About this support\n- Pay a lower levy of $60 per month if you live with an eligible person\n- Levy concession can only be granted for one MDW per eligible person and is capped at two levy concessions per household\n\n## Who is this for?\nIf you live with any of the following eligible person who is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident:\n\n- Child below 16 years old\n- Elderly person who is at least 67 years old\n- Person with disabilities (PWD) who must be certified by Singapore-registered doctor or an approved healthcare professional to permanently require some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):\n  - Washing\n  - Dressing\n  - Feeding\n  - Toileting\n  - Walking or moving around\n  - Transferring\n\n## How to apply?\nBefore hiring an MDW, you are required to obtain an approval from the [Ministry of Manpower (MOM)](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-domestic-worker/eligibility-and-requirements/employer-requirements) to hire an MDW.\n\nIf the eligible person is a PWD, you will also need to apply for the scheme:\n\n- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)\n\n- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)\n\nNo application for the scheme is further needed if:\n\n- You or your spouse is at least 67 years old\n- Your child is below 16 years old\n\nThe levy concession will automatically start once you meet the eligibility criteria and complete the required steps listed on [MOM’s website](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-domestic-worker/foreign-domestic-worker-levy/levy-concession).\n\nIf you were not automatically granted the levy concession, you can submit a form to check why:\n\nEligible Person\nForm\nChild\n[Check why levy concession for a child was not granted](https://go.gov.sg/check-lc-child)\nElderly or PWD\n[Check why levy concession for an elderly or PWD was not granted](https://go.gov.sg/check-lc-elderly-pwd)\n\n## Agency website\nFor more information that are PWD related: [View more details](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Migrant-Domestic-Worker-Levy-Concession)\n\nFor more information that are non-PWD related: [View more details](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-domestic-worker/foreign-domestic-worker-levy/levy-concession#who-can-qualify)\n\n## Email / Form\nFor enquiries that are PWD related: [Submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg)\n\nFor enquiries that are non-PWD related: [Submit an enquiry](https://www.mom.gov.sg/contact-us/feedback-and-enquiries)\n\n## Phone number\nFor enquiries that are PWD related: \nAIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060)\n\nFor enquiries that are non-PWD related: \nMOM Hotline: [6438 5122](tel:64385122)\n\nCalls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.",
