    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Financial support and benefits, Healthcare and well-being\n\n# Interim Disability Assistance Scheme for the Elderly (IDAPE)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/IDAPE*\n\nProvides monthly cash payout for elderly Singapore Citizens with severe disabilities who are not eligible for ElderShield.\n\n## Highlights\n- Receive $150 or $250 monthly cash payout for up to 72 months\n- Processing time take between 6 to 8 weeks\n- Apply through AIC’s eService for Financing Schemes (eFASS)\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Keywords:** Cash assistance, PWDs, Seniors\n\n## About this support\nSupports severely disabled seniors who are not eligible for ElderShield due to age or pre-existing disabilities, with monthly cash payouts of $150 or $250 for up to 72 months.\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Born on or before 30 September 1932 or\n- Born between 1 October 1932 and 30 September 1962 (both dates inclusive), with pre-existing disabilities as of 30 September 2002\n- Singapore Citizen living in Singapore\n- Monthly household income per person of $3,600 or less (annual value of property under $21,00 for households with no income)\n- Monthly payout depends on the monthly household income per person:\n  Monthly Household Income Per Person\n  Payout Amount\n  $0-$2,600\n  $250\n  $2,601 - $3,600\n  $150\n- Not be a [CareShield Life](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/CareShield-Life) or [ElderShield](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/ElderShield) policyholder/ supplement plan policyholder, or have made any claims before\n\n## How to apply?\nYou can apply:\n\n- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)\n- Via assistance from the nursing home your loved one is staying in\n- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)\n\nYou will need to contact an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor for a Severe Disability Assessment (SDA) as part of the application. Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) for a list of assessors.\n\n## Where to go\n[Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Interim-Disability-Assistance-Programme-for-the-Elderly)\n\n## Email / Form\n[Submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg)\n\n## Phone number\nAIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060)\n\nCalls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits\n\n# Enabling Transport Subsidy (ETS)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/ETS*\n\nSupports eligible Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with disabilities who need to use dedicated transport provided by the Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to access the Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC), Special Education (SPED) schools, Day Activity Centres (DACs), Sheltered Workshops (SWs), Special Student Care Centres (SSCCs), Enabling Skills for Life Programme (ESLP), Enabling Business Hubs (EBHs) and Enabling Service Hubs (ESHs).\n\n## Highlights\n- Up to 80% means-tested subsidy for transport fees\n- From July 2026, additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in 1969 or earlier\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities\n**Keywords:** Lower-income, PWDs, Subsidies\n\n## About this support\nUp to 80% means-tested subsidy for transport fees\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Singapore Citizen (SC) and Permanent Resident (PR)\n- Monthly household income per capita of $4,800 and below for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents\n- Annual Value (AV) of residence reflected on NRIC of $21,000 and below for households with no income\n- Persons with disabilities on transport services provided by SSAs and attending Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC), Special Education (SPED) schools, Day Activity Centres (DACs), Sheltered Workshops (SWs), Special Student Care Centres (SSCCs), Enabling Skills for Life Programme (ESLP), Enabling Business Hubs (EBHs) and Enabling Service Hubs (ESHs).\n\nFrom Jul 2026, SCs and PRs with monthly household income per capita of up to $4,800 will qualify for ETS.\n\n## How to apply?\nApply through SPED schools or SSAs that are arranging your transportation services. They will assist in conducting a means test for you and submit the subsidy request to SG Enable on your behalf.\n\n## Where to go\n[Enabling Village](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)\n[20 Lengkok Bahru](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)\n[#01-01, Singapore 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/transport/enabling-transport-subsidy)\n\n## Email / Form\n[contactus@sgenable.sg](mailto:contactus@sgenable.sg)\n\n## Phone number\nSG Enable Hotline: [1800-8585-885](tel:18008585885)",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support, Financial support and benefits\n\n# Taxi Subsidy Scheme (TSS)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/TSS*\n\nFor persons with permanent disabilities who are medically certified as unable to take public transport and totally dependent on taxi for travel to school, work or SG Enable-supported training.\n\n## Highlights\n- Up to 80% means-tested subsidy for taxi travel for the purpose of school, work or employment-related training supported by SG Enable\n- From July 2026, additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969\n- Application will be processed within 15 working days upon complete document submission \n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities\n**Keywords:** Lower-income, PWDs, Subsidies\n\n## About this support\nPersons with disabilities can apply for the means-tested subsidy for taxi travel for the purpose of school, work or employment-related training supported by SG Enable. The approved subsidy percentage* applies to the total fare for each trip (which covers additional charges such as booking fees, peak period surcharges and ERP charges).\n\nThe subsidy amounts will depend on:\n\n- Whether applicants are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents\n- Per capita monthly household income (PCHI)\n\n* subjected to means testing and meeting eligibility criteria\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents\n- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:\n  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment\n  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye\n  - Intellectual disability\n  - Autism\n  Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.\n- Certified as unable to take public transport and totally dependent on taxi for travel\n- Currently schooling, working, or attending employment-related training supported by SG Enable\n- Monthly Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) of $4,800 and below\n- Annual Value (AV) of residence reflected on NRIC of $21,000 and below for households with no income\n- Currently not owning any motor vehicles\n\nFrom July 2026, individuals with monthly per capita household income of $3,601 to $4,800 will also qualify for TSS.\n\n## How to apply?\nFor more information on the application process, please visit the [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/transport/taxi-subsidy-scheme).\n\n## Where to go\n[Enabling Village  20 Lengkok Bahru  #01-01, Singapore 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/transport/taxi-subsidy-scheme)\n\n## Email / Form\n[contactus@sgenable.sg](mailto:contactus@sgenable.sg)\n\n## Phone number\nSG Enable hotline: [1800-8585-885](tel:1800-8585-885)",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters\n\n# Equipment Rental Scheme (ERS)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/QEAKpruj*\n\nSubsidises the rental of essential care equipment for patients with serious illnesses.\n\n## Highlights\n- Subsidised weekly rental fees for essential medical equipment\n- Covers up to two-way transport and essential consumables\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Keywords:** Home healthcare, Palliative care\n\n## About this support\nThe Equipment Rental Scheme (ERS) provides patients with serious illnesses who have a prognosis of less than a year with the following subsidies:\n\n- Weekly rental fees for approved equipment such as wheelchair/pushchair, hospital bed, oxygen concentrator, pressure relief mattress and commode\n- Cost of two-way transport for delivery and collection of rented equipment\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident\n- Currently receiving care from a palliative care provider, whether home-based or in a public healthcare institution (PHI).\n- Diagnosed to have a serious illness with a prognosis of less than a year.\n- Assessed by a qualified assessor on the type(s) of equipment required.\n- *Must not be receiving subsidies for the same or similar equipment through other Government assistance schemes.\n\n*If you have previously received Government assistance or subsidies for same or similar type of equipment prior to your ERS application, eligibility to rent equipment(s) under ERS will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.\n\n## How to apply?\nApproach the [home palliative care provider](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Home-Palliative-Care) or PHI you are receiving care from to apply for ERS.\n\nIf you are currently not under the care of any home palliative care provider or PHI, you can reach out to [Singapore Hospice Council](https://www.singaporehospice.org.sg/#contact-pop).\n\n## Where to go\n[Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/about-us/aic-link-locations/)\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Equipment-Rental-Scheme)\n\n## Email / Form\n[Submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg)\n\n## Phone number\nAIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:1800-650-6060)\n\nCalls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Healthcare and well-being\n\n# Day Activity Centre (DAC)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-DACD*\n\nCommunity-based facilities that provide care and skills training to persons with disabilities aged 18 and above to maximise their independence.\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR\n**Keywords:** Day Care, Fees payable, Referral required\n\n## About this support\n- The DACs' programme is designed to equip persons with disabilities with daily living skills and community living skills to maximise their independence.\n- The activities also aim to meaningfully occupy persons with disabilities with social and recreational activities.\n- Therapeutic and behavioural intervention services may be provided at some centres.\n- DACs also provide a form of respite for caregivers during the day.\n\n## Who is this for?\nApplicants should be:\n\n- 18 years old and above*^#\n- Singapore citizens or Permanent Residents^^\n- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:\n  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment\n  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye\n  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear\n  - Intellectual disability\n  - Autism\n\nProof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)** completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.\n\n- Applicants should not be suffering from any untreated infectious disease.\n\n*Students of Government and community-funded SPED schools should be encouraged to remain in school until graduation. Parents of SPED graduands may approach their School to discuss the transition plans of the children prior to graduating from School.\n\n^Applicants who are below age 21 will need consent of parents or legal guardians for their application.\n\n#Applicants who are aged 21 and above with no mental capacity, will need the consent of the appointed deputy(s)/donee(s) on behalf of the applicant.\n\n^^For Permanent Residents, at least one immediate family member must be a Singapore Citizen. Immediate family members refer to spouses, parents, children or the applicant, including stepparents and stepchildren.\n\n**From 8 September 2025, the [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) is the standardised proof of disability required to verify an individual’s disability status when applying for selected MSF disability schemes and services and other selected Government schemes. Applicants can check if their disability status is already verified via their Touchpoints, SupportGoWhere, or call SG Enable at [1800-8585-885](tel:1800-8585-885)\n\n## How to apply?\n- Please approach a social service professional from a touchpoint (e.g. Social Service Agency (SSA), hospitals etc.) for assistance in submitting a DAC application. If you are currently not receiving support from any social service or medical touchpoints, you may [approach SG Enable for assistance](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/information-and-referral-services).\n- Before meeting your Touchpoints, all applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If you do not have a verified disability status, the Touchpoint will guide you to the relevant registered healthcare professionals to assist with DVF.\n\n**Submission of applications to SG Enable by Social Service Professional (Online or Hardcopy)**\n\n**Step 1:**\n\nAll applicants should check if they have a verified disability status by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with their Singpass. If the applicant already has a verified disability status, a DVF is not required.\n\n**Step 2:**\n\nIf the applicant does not have a verified disability status or has a new disability condition which has not been verified previously, registered Touchpoint Assessor/Admin must submit a copy of the DVF completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional together with the AD application.\n\n**Step 3:**\n\nRegistered touchpoints’ Assessor/Admin may submit clients’ AD application and completed DVF online via CorpPass (recommended) or via hardcopy.\n\n1. **Online submission (Recommended)**\n  Log into e-Services using your CorpPass\n2. **Hardcopy submission**\n  Download the [AD application form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/ad-application-form.pdf?sfvrsn=71d5f444_3), print and send together with the required documents. If required, you may download sections of the AD application form and DVF below for use:\n  - [Client Assessment Form (Revised)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-caf-r-form.pdf?sfvrsn=c2d096c3_1)\n  - [Medical Information Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-interim-medical-information.pdf?sfvrsn=c4f804d4_1)\n  - [Declaration Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/declaration-form.pdf?sfvrsn=a7fa3568_2)\n  - [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)\n\n## What to expect?\n- SG Enable will contact you within 10 working days upon receiving the completed application together with the required supporting documents from the touchpoint. SG Enable will also update the social worker who assisted in the application on the status of the application.\n- Acceptance into the programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies and approval of the centre management.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Active Ageing, Caregiving, Caregiving support, Counselling and crisis support, Disability support, Mental health\n\n# Community Mental Health Services\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/oWweAQMH*\n\nCommunity mental health teams located across Singapore provide support and access to mental health care for those in need.\n\n**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS\n**Keywords:** Counselling, Intervention and Therapy, Social-emotional Support\n\n## About this support\nMental health support services are offered by over 100 community mental health teams islandwide, with at least 1 team in every neighbourhood. These teams serve as the first stop for in-person mental health support.\n\n## Who is this for?\nAnyone aged 12 and above, and in need of mental health support.\n\n## How to apply?\n- Visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Community-Mental-Health-Services) to search for service providers by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.\n- Contact the team directly for an appointment.\n\nFor further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).\n\n- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.\n- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.\n\n## What to expect?\n- Every visit is strictly confidential.\n- Trained care professionals in each team will help identify your needs, develop a personalised care plan and provide support such as counselling and therapy.\n- They can also help to escalate and make necessary referrals if needed.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support\n\n# Assisted Deputyship Application Programme (ADAP) \n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/ddXZpncg*\n\nADAP supports caregivers of children without mental capacity to apply to be court-appointed deputies, through the simplified deputyship process. As a deputy, the caregiver can make legal decisions for the child when he/she turns 21.\n\n## Highlights\n- Guidance provided for simplified deputyship applications for caregivers of persons with disabilities and without mental capacity\n- Acceptance of mental capacity assessment reports from SPED Schools, DACs, SWs, or the MSF-appointed ADAP Agency\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities\n**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Referral required, Special needs\n\n## About this support\n- Programme provides guidance/facilitation, for caregivers of persons with no mental capacity to manage their own matters in adulthood, to apply to Family Justice Courts to be appointed as legal deputies for their child. This is a simplified process that is also more affordable, compared to application for deputyship under standard route.\n- Courts may accept mental capacity assessment reports prepared by psychologists from Special Education Schools (SPED Schools), selected Day Activity Centres (DACs), Sheltered Workshops (SWs), or the MSF-appointed ADAP Agency in lieu of a medical report. This applies only when the child is enrolled in a SPED school, DAC, or SW that is onboard the ADAP programme. In all other cases, the mental capacity assessment must be conducted by a medical capacity assessment must be conducted by a medical doctor or psychiatrist.\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Your child is:\n  - between 18 and 21 years old as well as in the graduating cohort in a Special Education (SPED) school; or\n  - above 18 years old and enrolled in an MSF-funded Day Activity Centre (DAC) or Sheltered Workshop (SW).\n- You agree to use the standard list of powers/orders available under the Integrated Family Application Management System (iFAMS) when filing a simplified Deputyship application.\n- All family members and any other caregivers agree for you to make the application (i.e. it is an uncontested case).\n\n## How to apply?\nCaregivers can approach the relevant staff in the SPED school, Day Activity Centre or Sheltered Workshop to indicate interest to apply for Deputyship. The school or centre will work with an MSF-appointed ADAP Agency to guide the parent/caregiver in their Deputyship application.\n\nFor Caregivers whose child with disability is not enrolled in a service, please contact ADAP Agency directly via phone or email for enquiries on deputyship application.\n\n## Where to go\nMINDS\nCaregivers Support Services Centre\n\n[11 Jalan Ubi Kembangan-chai Chee Community Hub 409074](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=409074)\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/assisted-deputyship-application-programme-(adap))\n\n## Email / Form\n[Submit an enquiry](mailto:fcp@minds.org.sg)\n\nReferral is required for application.\n\n## Phone number\nADAP Agency Hotline: 6547 8503",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Healthcare and well-being\n\n# Dementia Day Care\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-DDC*\n\nMind stimulating activities, exercises and personal care at day care centres for seniors with dementia.\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS\n**Keywords:** Day Care, Referral required, Subsidies\n\n## About this support\nServices at day care centres help seniors with mild to advanced dementia continue living in the community and delay the need for institutionalisation. They include:\n\n- Group and individual activities to slow down deterioration of physical and mental functions (based on their abilities)\n- Individualised care plans for seniors with suitable maintenance exercises\n- Assistance with daily personal care\n- Caregiver support activities (e.g. support groups, talks and care demonstrations, etc)\n- Offered on weekdays, but some centres also provide weekend support\n\n## Who is this for?\nSenior diagnosed with mild to advanced dementia, and/or require supervision during the day while their caregivers are at work.\n\n## How to apply?\nYou can apply:\n\n- Through the hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs\n- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)\n\nIf you are interested to view the list of service providers, visit the [AIC’s website](https://aic.sg/Care-Services/Day-Care).\n\nFor further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).\n\n- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.\n- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.\n\n## What to expect?\nSubsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/care-services/home-medical#faq) result.\n\n- Only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support\n\n# Inpatient Hospice Palliative Care Service (IHPCS)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-IHPCS*\n\nSupports end-of-life patients who cannot be cared for at home and require inpatient care.\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS\n**Keywords:** Palliative care, Referral required\n\n## About this support\nProvides medical and emotional support for end-of-life patients who cannot be cared for at home and their caregivers, including services provided by specialised care teams such as:\n\n- Specialist palliative care focusing on the management of symptoms such as pain, breathlessness, nausea and vomiting\n- Emotional, spiritual and grief support and counselling\n- Palliative rehabilitation, including physiotherapy and occupational therapy\n- Music and art therapy\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Patient with a prognosis of less than 3 months who needs:\n  - Specialised care especially in the last phase of life, when care at home, in a nursing home or outpatient setting is not possible.\n\n- Patient with a prognosis of less than 12 months who requires:\n  - Time-limited care up to 28 calendar days for severe symptoms that cannot be managed in outpatient settings\n\n## How to apply?\nYou can apply:\n\n- Through the hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs\n- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)\n\nIf you are interested to view the list of service providers, visit the [AIC’s website](https://aic.sg/Care-Services/Inpatient-Hospice-Palliative-Care-Services) .\n\nFor further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).\n\n- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.\n- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.\n\n## What to expect?\n- Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/care-services/home-medical#faq) result.\n  - Only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents\n- MediShield Life and MediSave can be used to cover costs.\n- If patients need further financial assistance, their respective service providers will be able to provide more information.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support\n\n# Nursing Home\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-NH*\n\nA long-term residential care facility for seniors who have limited or no caregiver support and require assistance with daily nursing and living needs.\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS\n**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Referral required\n\n## About this support\nProvides round-the-clock nursing and care services, including:\n\n- Help with daily living activities such as going to the toilet, showering, eating, etc\n- Nursing support such as management of nasogastric tube, urine catheter, wound dressing, etc\n- Physical and social activities such as maintenance exercises, outings, etc\n\nFor selected nursing homes with dementia and/or psychiatric facilities, services include:\n\n- Programmes and activities for cognitive stimulation to slow down the deterioration of the senior’s physical and mental functions\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Senior who has a physical or mental disability because of illness\n- Unable to be cared for at home by family or paid domestic worker, and has tried all other care options such as using day care, home medical, home nursing services, etc\n\n## How to apply?\nYou can apply:\n\n- Through the hospital, polyclinic or medical social worker who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs\n- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)\n\nIf you are interested to view the list of providers, visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Nursing-Home).\n\nFor further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).\n\n- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.\n- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.\n\n## What to expect?\n- Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/Care-Services/nursing-home#faq) result.\n  - Only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents\n  - Additional fees such as deposits and other charges may apply.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Healthcare and well-being\n\n# Home Nursing\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-HN*\n\nNursing services provided at home for seniors who are unable to leave their homes.\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS\n**Keywords:** Home Care, Referral required\n\n## About this support\nHome visits by nurses to help seniors who are unable to leave their homes with:\n\n- Vital signs monitoring (e.g. blood pressure and blood sugar levels)\n- Caregiving training\n- Care coordination\n- Medication management\n- Nursing care (e.g. injections, wound dressing and tube changes)\n\n## Who is this for?\nHomebound seniors and their caregivers who need help with nursing care at home.\n\n## How to apply?\nYou can apply:\n\n- Through the hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs\n- At any of the [AIC Links](https://aic.sg/Contact-Us)\n\nIf you are interested to view the list of service providers, visit the [AIC’s website](https://aic.sg/Care-Services/Home-Nursing).\n\nFor further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or submit an enquiry.\n\n- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.\n- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.\n\n## What to expect?\nSubsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/care-services/home-medical#faq) result.\n\n- Only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Healthcare and well-being\n\n# Maintenance Day Care Centre\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-MDCC*\n\nFull day programme of engaging activities, exercises and personal care for seniors at day care centres.\n\n**Who it targets:** Seniors\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS\n**Keywords:** Day Care, Referral required, Subsidies\n\n## About this support\n- Centre-based day care that supports seniors in ageing well in the community, as well providing support and respite for their family/caregivers\n- Provides programmes and care support services for seniors at day care centres, such as:\n  - Meals (e.g. lunch and tea break)\n  - Basic nursing and health services\n  - Suitable maintenance exercises that are created for seniors based on their Individualised Care Plan\n  - Social and recreational activities (e.g. arts & crafts, games and karaoke sessions)\n  - Personal care (e.g. bathing and getting dressed)\n  - Mostly offered on weekdays, but some centres also provide weekend support\n\n## Who is this for?\nSeniors suitable for centre-based care setting during the day, and/or require supervision while their caregivers are at work.\n\n## How to apply?\n- You can apply:\n  ·       Through the hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs\n  ·       At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)\n  If you are interested to view the list of service providers, visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Day-Care).\n  For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or[ submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).\n  - Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.\n  - Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.\n\n## What to expect?\nSubsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/care-services/home-medical#faq) result.\n\n- Only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters\n\n# Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC) Rebate\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SCCR*\n\nQuarterly rebates to offset S&CC fees for HDB households. Eligible households will receive 1.5 to 3.5 months of the GST Voucher (GSTV) – S&CC Rebate.\n\n## Highlights\n- 1.5 to 3.5 months of S&CC Rebate in each Financial Year\n- Rebates will be given out in January, April, July and October\n- No application needed\n\n**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable\n**Keywords:** Budget 2024, HDB households, Rebates\n\n## About this support\n- Offsets between 1.5 and 3.5 months of S&CC\n- Eligible households will receive their S&CC rebates in January, April, July, and October\n\n## Who is this for?\nA HDB household will be eligible for the S&CC rebate if all the criteria below are fulfilled:\n\n- There must be at least one Singapore Citizen flat owner or occupier in the flat\n- The flat owner(s) and essential occupier(s) of the flat do not own or have any interest in a private property\n- The flat owner(s) have not rented out the whole flat\n\n## How to apply?\n- No application required\n- S&CC rebates will be credited directly to your household's S&CC account managed by your respective Town Council\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.govbenefits.gov.sg/)\n\n## Email / Form\nHDB residents can check or enquire about their household's eligibility for GSTV – S&CC Rebate using these e-Services for [purchased flats](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/AG10AWScRebate/AG10SRebatesMain) and [rental flats](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/AG10AWScRebate/AG10SRentalRebatesMain).",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support\n\n# Caregiver Training and Support Programme\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-CTCP*\n\nProvides training and support to caregivers of persons with mental health conditions so that they can better cope with their caregiving duties.\n\n**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR\n**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Free\n\n## About this support\nCTSP consists of the Caregivers-to-Caregivers (C2C) Programme and Engagement-to-Empowerment (E2E) Programme. C2C aims to provide caregivers with the knowledge and skills regarding caregiving so that they can better cope with their caregiving duties.\n\nC2C provides various types of training courses that range from 8 to 12 sessions and in 3 different languages, to cover general or specific mental health conditions. Through the C2C training courses, caregiver leaders are also identified and trained to volunteer as caregiver leaders to support other caregivers in subsequent C2C classes and /or outreach and advocacy work.\n\nE2E consists of the following components:\n\n- Caregiver-for-Caregiver (C4C) Support Programme: 12 support group sessions over a year, with the aim of increasing support networks for caregivers. The first six sessions will be held in-person and will aim to provide support and equip caregivers with coping skills. Subsequent sessions may be a mix of online or in-person sessions, including self-run activities by caregivers with support from Mindfull Community Limited staff, to gather fellow caregivers for social activities or a sharing session.\n- Train-the-Trainer (TTT): Caregivers who indicated interest to contribute and identified by staff as having potential are coached and trained as Volunteer Trainers and/or to support advocacy and outreach work through “Train-the-Trainer” modules so they can volunteer to support CAL’s programmes and activities.\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Caregivers of Persons with Mental Health Issues (PMHIs).\n- This can range from spouses, partners, parents, siblings, grandchildren, friends, neighbours, etc of someone who is experiencing a mental health condition.\n\n## How to apply?\nRegister online through the [form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=mH6MQ8-ncE-ro_WXOpzXWwTicfzzzZ1Jqtl-rNfRemJUMEpJWUo4NFFQVjZMWDE4NEs3N1hPWTBHNiQlQCN0PWcu&route=shorturl).\n\n## What to expect?\nAfter registration, interested participants will receive a call and email from Mindfull Community Limited to confirm their registration.[form](https://forms.office.com/pages/responsepage.aspx?id=mH6MQ8-ncE-ro_WXOpzXWwTicfzzzZ1Jqtl-rNfRemJUMEpJWUo4NFFQVjZMWDE4NEs3N1hPWTBHNiQlQCN0PWcu&route=shorturl)",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Counselling and crisis support, Education and learning, Family, parenting and relationships, Mental health\n\n# SAMH Youthreach\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-SY*\n\nProvides psychosocial support and recovery programmes for youths aged 13 to 21 with emotional, psychological and psychiatric issues in the community.\n\n**Who it targets:** Vulnerable\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR\n**Keywords:** Counselling, Free, Referral required\n\n## About this support\nThe programme staff work with youths and their families to minimise risk, promote safety and improve functioning.\n\nServices include:\n\n- Counselling Case Management\n- Family Psychoeducation Programme\n- Expressive Therapies\n- Psycho-social Activities\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents aged 13 to 21 with emotional, psychological and/or psychiatric issues.\n- No recent history of violent behaviour, alcohol or substance abuse, or sexual acting out behaviour.\n- Willing to participate in the centre's activities.\n- Family is willing to participate in case management and family education programmes.\n\n## How to apply?\nReferral by a psychiatrist, school counsellor, or social worker using the SAMH referral form is required.\n\n## What to expect?\n- An intake interview with child/youth and caregiver will be arranged to assess suitability.\n- Upon successful registration, the child/youth and caregiver will be engaged for services including case management, psychoeducation and psychosocial development programmes.",
    "sections": {/* Lines 1097-1101 omitted */}

    "title": "Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)",
    "description": "A legal document that allows you (the 'Donor') to appoint one or more trusted persons (the 'Donee') to  make decisions on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Legacy planning, Retirement and legacy planning\n\n# Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-LPA*\n\nA legal document that allows you (the 'Donor') to appoint one or more trusted persons (the 'Donee') to  make decisions on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity.\n\n**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS\n**Keywords:** Advance Care Planning, Fees payable\n\n## About this support\nAn LPA allows you to appoint trusted individuals to make decisions on (i) personal welfare and (ii) property and affairs, on your behalf in the event you lose mental capacity.\n\n## Who is this for?\nDonors must:\n\n- Be 21 years old and above\n- Have the mental capacity to make your own decisions\n- Not be an undischarged bankrupt if you wish to make an LPA for property and affairs matters\n\nDonees must:\n\n- Be 21 years old and above\n- Be your spouse or partner, family member or relative, friend, or a licensed trust company for property and affair matters only\n- Have the mental capacity to make their own decisions\n\n## How to apply?\nYou can:\n\n- [Apply online](https://opg-eservice.msf.gov.sg/) or\n- You may also [book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) or visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) today for in-person guidance and assistance\n  for your application. Please note that a [LPA certificate issuer](https://book.health.gov.sg/lpa) is required to ensure that the donor has the mental capacity to make a LPA.\n\n## What to expect?\nHere are the steps on how to make an LPA:\n\n- Step 1: Decide on the type of LPA form\n  - LPA Form 1 grants general powers to Donee(s) who will make decisions on your behalf when you lose mental capacity\n  - LPA Form 2 is for applicants who want to appoint more than 2 Donees and/or more than 1 replacement Donee, and grant specific or customised powers that are not in the scope of LPA Form 1. You will need to engage a lawyer for LPA Form 2.\n- Step 2: [Find an LPA certificate issuer ](https://book.health.gov.sg/lpa)who is:\n  - A medical professional accredited by the OPG\n  - A registered psychiatrist\n  - A practising lawyer (excluding lawyers registered under section 36E of the Legal Profession Act 1966)\n- You and the LPA certificate issuer must digitally sign the LPA using the Singpass app. Your Donees can sign electronically by accepting their appointment.\n- For your LPA to be legally valid, the certificate issuer must submit the LPA application to Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) via OPG Online (OPGO), as authorised by you.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support, Financial support and benefits, Retirement and legacy planning\n\n# Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SNSS*\n\nEnables parents to set aside CPF savings for the long-term care of children with special needs.\n\n## Highlights\n- Parents may nominate child to receive payouts from their CPF savings after they pass on\n- Minimum monthly payout is $250, parents may decide on a higher amount\n- Submit the application and supporting documents to SNTC via email or mail\n\n**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities\n**Keywords:** CPF payouts, Parents, Special needs\n\n## About this support\n- Parents may nominate child with special needs to receive payouts from their CPF savings after death with minimum monthly payout of $250.\n- If the nominating parent’s CPF savings upon his/her demise is insufficient to support a year’s worth of payout (e.g. a minimum monthly payout is S$250 x 12 months = S$3,000), the CPF savings will be disbursed as a lump sum to the nominee with special needs.\n\n## Who is this for?\nThe nominating applicant should be:\n\n- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident\n- The parent or an appointed legal guardian of the child with special needs\n\nThe child with special needs should:\n\n- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:\n  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment\n  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye\n  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear\n  - Intellectual disability\n  - Autism\n\nProof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.\n\n**Or**\n\n- is attending or had attended a Special Education School\n\nThe 6 ADLs are:\n\n- Eating\n- Bathing\n- Dressing\n- Transferring\n- Toileting\n- Walking or moving around\n\n## How to apply?\nBefore proceeding, all applicants are encouraged to check if your child’s disability status has already been verified.\n\nFind out more here: https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification\n\nYou can apply by submitting the completed [application form](https://www.sgenable.sg/snss) and supporting documents:\n\n- via mail to Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), Future Care Planning Resource Centre by SG Enable, 22 Lengkok Bahru, Vista, Enabling Village #03-03  Singapore 159824\n- via email to [futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg).\n\nYou'll need to provide copies of:\n\n- Nominating applicant's and child's NRIC\n- Child's Birth Certificate\n\nIf your child's disability status has not been verified:\n\n- Supporting document from the SPED school issued on the school’s official letterhead stating that the Person with Special Needs (PSN) is currently attending or has previously attended the SPED school or\n- [Disability Verification Form (DVF) ](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)completed by a Registered Healthcare Professional*\n\nAfter mailing the application and upon approval by MSF, parents will receive an eligibility letter, which they should bring to the CPF Board to make the SNSS nomination.\n\n*Please note that a submitted Disability Verification Form (DVF) does not mean that your child’s disability status has been verified.\n\n## Where to go\n[22 Lengkok Bahru 159824](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159824)\n\nFuture Care Planning Resource Centre by SG Enable,\n\nEnabling Village #03-03\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.sntc.org.sg/services/special-needs-savings-scheme-(snss))\n\n## Email / Form\n[futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg)\n\n## Phone number\nSpecial Needs Savings Scheme Hotline:\n\n[6278 9598](tel:62789598)\n\n(Operating hours: 9am-6pm on weekdays, closed on weekends and public holidays)",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support\n\n# CAREwell\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/izIXWd7S*\n\nCAREwell is a program that supports caregivers in their caregiving role, emotional and mental wellness, decision- making regarding services, and care management.\n\n## Highlights\n- Each family is guided by a transdisciplinary CAREwell Key Worker.\n- CAREwell Key Workers meet with caregiver for needs analysis and establish family support plan.\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities\n**Keywords:** Caregiver support\n\n## About this support\nCAREwell offers tailored support to caregivers through a combination of approaches:\n\n1. Trauma-informed emotional support and mental health advisory for caregivers\n2. Professional support on service navigation, care coordination, and service integration for meeting dependent and family’s social and health needs.\n\nEach family is paired with a Keyworker, a trained professional in social work, healthcare, special needs, or related fields. The Keyworker will work with the caregiver to assess needs and identify challenges, establish a family support plan, and implement strategies to support both the caregiver and their dependent.\n\n## Who is this for?\nCAREwell program is a highly subsidised program made affordable to all caregivers of persons with special needs.\n\nInterested caregivers are encouraged to get in touch with us to find out the eligible subsidies available to them.\n\n## How to apply?\nInterested caregivers or external agency can click on the request link for CAREwell. For caregivers, you will receive an email with a link to ‘CSG Caregiver Needs Form’. Fill in the form and our team will contact you shortly.\n\nApplicants to CAREwell are screened for suitability before being enrolled into the programme.\n\n## Where to go\n[20 Lengkok Bahru 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)\n#03-06/07 Block Vista\n\n## Agency website\nhttps://caring.sg/carewell\n\n## Email / Form\n[https://www.caring.sg/contact-us](https://www.caring.sg/contact-us/)",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support\n\n# CAREconnect\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/bncVrBSn*\n\nCAREconnect offers inclusive social events for family bonding and connection to fellow caregivers and volunteers, through mobilising support groups, organising inclusive, social, and/or respite events, and webinars.\n\n## Highlights\n- CAREconnect goes beyond just offering services. It’s a community movement because it aims to build a network of support for caregivers within their local neighborhoods.\n- CAREconnect conducts inclusive events for caregivers. 92% of caregivers agreed that the events helped them to feel more included in their neighbourhood.\n- The monthly webinars focus on a variety of topics and resources that would help caregivers make informed decisions and provide some answers to questions and difficulties they may have. 82% of caregivers at CAREconnect Webinars agreed that the sessions were helpful in learning to care for their child better.\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities\n**Keywords:** Caregiver support\n\n## About this support\nCAREconnect offers a variety of events to cater to different needs and preferences:\n\n- Informative Webinars: CAREconnect offers online webinars that provide valuable caregiving resources and information, accessible from the comfort of home.\n- Engaging Physical Events: CAREconnect organizes face-to-face events, in collaboration with volunteers and grassroots organizations, offering caregivers the opportunity to connect, share experiences, and receive emotional support.\n\nBy offering both online and in-person events, along with strong community ties through volunteers and grassroots organizations, CAREconnect builds an inclusive and accessible support system for caregivers.\n\nBeyond just offering services, CAREconnect is a community movement focused on creating a support network for caregivers within their local neighborhoods. Partnership with grassroots enhances CAREconnect’s ability to reach a broader audience and address the unique challenges caregivers face.\n\n## Who is this for?\nCaregivers of persons with special needs.\n\n## How to apply?\nClick CaringSG event link to view available events. Registration information can be found at each individual event page.\n\n## Where to go\n[20 Lengkok Bahru 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)\n#03-06/07 Block Vista\n\n## Agency website\nhttps://www.facebook.com/CaringSGLtd/\n\n## Email / Form\nhttps://www.caring.sg/contact-us/",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support\n\n# Step One\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/PrBDGZa7*\n\nProgramme that equips caregivers of young children up to 7 years old diagnosed with developmental delay / disability with knowledge and skills to support their loved ones and themselves.\n\n## Highlights\n- Free programme\n- Access to bite-sized, self paced e-learning modules\n- Regular ‘Ask-Me-Anything’ online support group sessions to learn practical strategies and tips from experienced caregivers on top-of-mind topics e.g. handling tantrums and meltdowns, supporting siblings, money matters\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities\n**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Parents, Special needs\n\n## About this support\nStep One programme helps you understand your child, find resources and learn strategies to help your child develop and grow and connects you with other caregivers for support. You can learn from experienced caregivers’ perspectives and be equipped with practical knowledge and skills, to ensure you are well-prepared and confident to start your caregiving journey.\n\n## Who is this for?\nCaregivers of young children up to 7 years old with developmental needs or disability (defined as autism, intellectual disability, physical disability, hearing loss, visual impairment and excludes learning disorders).\n\nCaregivers or child(ren) should be Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents.\n\n## How to apply?\nSign up with CaringSG at [https://caring.sg/stepone](https://caring.sg/stepone/)\n\n## Where to go\n[20 Lengkok Bahru 159053](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=159053)\nEnabling Village #03-06/07 Block Vista\n\n## Agency website\n[https://caring.sg/stepone](https://caring.sg/stepone/)\n\n## Email / Form\n[https://caring.sg/contact-us](https://caring.sg/contact-us/)",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving support, Disability support\n\n# Take-a-Break (TAB)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/JqJOoLnT*\n\nTake-a-Break (TAB) is a respite care programme to provide caregivers temporary relief from their caregiving responsibilities. \n\nBased on their needs, caregivers may choose from a range of home-based respite care services and determine the frequency of service over a specific duration. \n\nSubsidies are available for eligible caregivers.\n\n## Highlights\n- Provides caregivers with temporary relief from caregiving responsibilities.\n- Offers flexibility in respite options, allowing caregivers to choose from a range of home-based respite care services that best suit their needs.\n\n**Who it targets:** Families, Persons with disabilities\n**Keywords:** Caregiver support, Parents, Special needs\n\n## About this support\n- Provide temporary relief for caregivers from their caregiving responsibilities, allowing them to rest, attend to personal needs, or manage other commitments\n\n- Offers flexibility in respite options, allowing caregivers to choose from a range of home-based respite care services that best suit their needs.\n\n## Who is this for?\n1. Caregiver or care recipient is a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident;\n2. Caregiver of persons with any one or more of the following disability types:\n\n- Autism\n- Intellectual Disability\n- Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment\n- Sensory Disability\n- Children and young persons with Developmental Needs and/or in EIPIC\n\n## How to apply?\nPlease approach a social service professional from a touchpoint (e.g. Social Service Agency (SSA), hospitals etc.) to apply.\n\nYou can contact email SPD directly if assistance is needed for applying to TAB.\n\nEmail: [Tab@spd.org.sg](mailto:Tab@spd.org.sg)\n\n## Where to go\n[2 Peng Nguan Street Spd Ability Centre 168955](https://onemap.gov.sg/?postal=168955)\n\n## Agency website\n[Take-A-Break (TAB) programme - SPD](https://www.spd.org.sg/what-we-do/social-support/take-a-break-tab-programme/)\n\n## Email / Form\n[Tab@spd.org.sg](mailto:Tab@spd.org.sg)\n\n## Phone number\nSPD: 6579 0796",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Financial support and benefits, Healthcare and well-being\n\n# Home Caregiving Grant (HCG)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/HCG*\n\nProvides financial support to help with caregiving expenses for households caring for persons with moderate to severe disabilities.\n\n## Highlights\n- Payouts of $200, $400 or $600 per month\n- Processing time takes up to 4 weeks\n- Apply through AIC’s eService portal (eFASS)\n\n**Who it targets:** Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Keywords:** Caregiving expenses, Cash assistance, PWDs\n\n## About this support\nMonthly cash payout of $200, $400 or $600\n\n## Who is this for?\nCare recipient must meet the following criteria:\n\n- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident with a parent, child or spouse who is a Singapore Citizen\n- Lives in Singapore\n- Always requires some assistance on a permanent basis with at least 3 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)\n- Monthly per capita household income of less than or equal to $4,800 or less  (or property annual value of $21,000 or below for households with no income)\n- Those with multiple properties will receive the lowest HCG payout of $200 per month\n- [Not in a residential long-term care institution](https://www.aic.sg/financial-assistance/home-caregiving-grant#q5a)\n\nThe 6 ADLs are:\n\n- Eating\n- Bathing\n- Dressing\n- Transferring\n- Toileting\n- Walking or moving around\n\n## How to apply?\nYou can apply:\n\n- Online at the [AIC eService Portal](https://efinance.aic.sg/)\n- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us)\n\nYou'll need to provide:\n\n- [Completed Functional Assessment Report](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/Functional-Assessment-Report.pdf) from your General Practitioner, a registered Nurse or a registered Physio/Occupational Therapist\n- NRIC details\n- Bank details\n\n## Where to go\n[Contact Us | AIC](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.aic.sg/financial-assistance/home-caregiving-grant)\n\n## Email / Form\n[Contact Us | AIC](https://www.aic.sg/contact-us)\n\n## Phone number\nAIC     "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters\n\n# Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/EASE*\n\nSubsidy for Singapore Citizen households with at least one senior who meets age criterion and needs help to install senior-friendly fittings.\n\n## Highlights\n- Up to 95% subsidy of improvement costs\n- Respond within 14 working days upon receipt of application\n- Apply via EASE e-Service or Mobile@HDB\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Keywords:** Seniors, Subsidies\n\n## About this support\n- Depending on your flat type, the subsidy can cover up to 95% of the total improvement cost.\n- ['Calculate Calculate Cost of HIP/ EASE Improvement Items' e-Service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/DJ02AWFNCALV7/Main)\n  - Choose ‘EASE (Direct Application)’ under the selection type, indicate your flat type and the EASE improvements you wish to have.\n- If you are a senior living in a rental flat, your preferred EASE improvement items will be fully funded by the Government.\n\n## Who is this for?\nSingapore Citizen household with a senior who is aged:\n\n- 65 and above; or\n- Between 60 and 64, and requires assistance for one or more of the Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):\n  - Eating\n  - Bathing\n  - Dressing\n  - Transferring\n  - Toileting\n  - Walking or moving around\n\n## How to apply?\nYou can apply:\n\n- [Apply for Enhancement for Active Seniors (EASE) Online via EASE](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BN37AWEASE/BN37PMain.jsp)\n- Mobile@HDB\n\nYou are required to submit a [Functional Assessment Report](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/-/media/managing-my-home/upgrading-and-redevelopment/enhancement-for-active-seniors-ease/FAR-Sep-2025.pdf) if you are a Singapore Citizen flat owner with at least one member in the household aged between 60 and 64 who requires assistance for one or more of the Activities of Daily Living (ADL)\n\n- The Functional Assessment Report for the elderly aged between 60 and 64 must be endorsed by a qualified assessor such as a Singapore Medical Council fully registered doctor, and must be submitted together with your application form\n\n## Where to go\n[Book an appointment via e-Appointment service](https://services2.hdb.gov.sg/webapp/BF13AWAppointmentWeb/branch/)\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/managing-my-home/upgrading-and-redevelopment/enhancement-for-active-seniors-ease)\n\n## Email / Form\n[Submit an enquiry](https://www.hdb.gov.sg/write-to-us)\n\n## Phone number\nHDB Branch Service Line: [6225-5432](tel:6225-5432)",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support\n\n# Enhanced Home Personal Care (HPC+)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/o0cdiebU*\n\nSupport frail or homebound seniors who require assistance with activities of daily living, and/or general support with routine tasks in the community.\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR\n**Keywords:** Home Care, Referral required, Seniors\n\n## About this support\nProvided by trained care professionals to assist seniors and their caregivers with:\n\n- Personal care needs\n  - Activities of Daily Living (e.g. showering, feeding)\n  - Mind stimulating activities\n  - Simple maintenance exercises prescribed by physiotherapist, occupational therapist, or speech therapist\n  - Elder-sitting and respite for caregivers\n- General support with routine tasks (e.g. regular check-ins, medication reminders, help with errands)\n- Monitoring and responding to falls 24/7 using digital devices the client has installed at home\n- Household chores (e.g. sweeping floors, cleaning fans and windows, and washing toilets)\n\n## Who is this for?\nSenior who:\n\n- Requires personal services to continue living well at home\n- Is a Singapore Citizen (SC), Permanent Resident (PR) or foreigner\n\nCaregiver who:\n\n- Needs support in their caregiving duties\n- Is a Singapore Citizen (SC), Permanent Resident (PR) or foreigner\n\n## How to apply?\n- You will need to get a referral from a hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved ones’ condition and needs.\n- You may also contact the service provider for a discussion. Visit the [Agency for Integrated Care (AIC)’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Enhanced-Home-Personal-Care) to search for service providers by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.\n- For further assistance, contact the AIC at [1800 650 6060](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-HPCSH/home-personal-care-hpc), email [enquiries@aic.sg](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg) or walk into a nearby [AIC Link](https://aic.sg/Contact-Us).\n\n## What to expect?\n- Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://www.aic.sg/care-services/home-personal-care#faq) result.\n  - Only applicable to SC and PR\n- Applicants for care services need to fulfil the services’ eligibility criteria and providers’ service boundaries, if any, and enrolments are subject to availability of vacancies.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support\n\n# Home Personal Care (HPC)\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-HPCSH*\n\nSupports frail or homebound seniors who require help with activities of daily living and/or housekeeping.\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR, OTHERS\n**Keywords:** Home Care, Referral required\n\n## About this support\nProvided by trained care professionals to assist seniors and their caregivers with:\n\n- Activities of Daily Living (e.g. showering, light housekeeping)\n- Medication\n- Mind stimulating activities\n- Elder-sitting and respite for caregivers\n- Light household chores (e.g. sweeping floors, cleaning fans and windows, and washing toilets)\n\n**Note**: From 1 April 2026, HPC will be enhanced to provide more tailored and frequent support for clients, including those with higher care needs. On top of the ADLs and IADLs support, enhanced HPC also provides new services such as technology-enabled monitoring to assure caregivers of the client’s safety at home. Refer to the [link](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/o0cdiebU/enhanced-home-personal-care-hpc) for more information regarding enhanced Home Personal Care.\n\n## Who is this for?\nSenior who:\n\n- Requires personal services to continue living well at home\n- Is a Singapore Citizen (SC), Permanent Resident (PR) or foreigner\n\nCaregiver who:\n\n- Needs support in their caregiving duties\n- Is a Singapore Citizen (SC), Permanent Resident (PR) or foreigner\n\n## How to apply?\n- You will need to get a referral from a hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved ones’ condition and needs.\n- You may also contact the service provider for a discussion. Visit [AIC’s website](https://aic.sg/Care-Services/Home-Personal-Care) to search for service providers by** **postal code, address or your device’s current location.\n- For further assistance, contact the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) at [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060), email [enquiries@aic.sg](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg) or walk in to a nearby [AIC Link](https://aic.sg/Contact-Us).\n\n## What to expect?\n- Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/care-services/home-personal-care#faq) result.\n  - Only applicable to SC and PR\n- Applicants for care services may need to fulfil the services’ eligibility criteria and providers’ service boundaries, if any, and enrolments are subject to availability of vacancies.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters\n\n# Enhancement for Active Seniors (Private Housing): EASE (Private) \n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/nzWStXJo*\n\nProvides subsidies to Singapore Citizen seniors living in private properties, for the installation of senior-friendly fittings.\n\n## Highlights\n- EASE (Private) will be in rolled out in phases from 1 April 2026, prioritising households with older seniors first\n- Apply via EASE (Private) portal\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Keywords:** Seniors, Subsidies\n\n## About this support\n- EASE (Private) provides subsidies for the installation of senior-friendly fittings in private properties, to improve the mobility and safety of seniors within their homes.\n- Eligible households will each receive $1,200 in vouchers that can be used to subsidise 75% of the cost of selected senior-friendly fittings purchased from appointed contractors. The household will only need to pay the remaining 25%.\n- The seven senior-friendly fittings and their prices are as follows:\n\n**Prices (after GST)**\n**Prices after 75% subsidy**\nSingle-Step Ramp\n$283.40\n$70.85\nHandrail\n$632.20\n$158.05\nGrab Bars\nFirst  set of 8 for combined toilet/bathroom or 10 pcs for separate toilet/bathroom\n$523.20\n$130.80\nSecond set onwards 6 pcs\n$305.20\n$76.30\nHome Fire Alarm Device\n$119.90\n$29.98\nBidet Spray\n$65.40\n$16.35\nSlip-Resistant Treatment to Existing Toilet Flooring*\n*The treatment is for size up to 3.5sqm. For non-standard bathroom sizes larger than 3.5 sqm, further assessment will be done during site survey by contractors.\n$239.80\n$59.95\nShower Seat\n$305.20\n$76.30\n\n## Who is this for?\nEASE (Private) is available to private property households with at least one Singaporean household member aged:\n\n1. 65 years old and above; or\n\n1. Between 60 and 64 years old requiring assistance with at least one of the Activities of Daily Living (ADL)*\n\n*ADL refers to daily self-care activities, including washing/bathing, dressing, feeding, toileting, mobility and transferring.\n\nSeniors aged 60 to 64 must submit a Functional Assessment Report endorsed by a qualified assessor, such as a doctor, registered nurse, or registered physiotherapist/occupational therapist.\n\n## How to apply?\nApplications for EASE (Private) will be rolled out in phases (based on age of seniors in the household in 2026):\n\n**When to Apply**\n**Who Can Apply**\n**From 1 Apr 2026 onwards**\nHouseholds with seniors aged 80 and above\nHouseholds with seniors aged 60 and above who require assistance with at least one of the Activities of Daily Living (ADL)\n**From 1 Jul 2026 onwards**\nHouseholds with seniors aged 70 and above\n**From 1 Oct 2026 onwards**\nHouseholds with seniors aged 65 and above\n\nLetters and SMSes will be progressively sent to eligible households to apply for EASE (Private).\n\nYou can apply via BCA’s [EASE (Private) Portal](https://go.gov.sg/ease-private).\n\nSeniors aged 60 to 64 who requires assistance for one or more of the Activities of Daily Living (ADL) must submit a [Functional Assessment Report](https://www.aic.sg/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/Functional-Assessment-Report.pdf) endorsed by a qualified assessor, such as a doctor, registered nurse or registered physiotherapist/occupational therapist.\n\n## Email / Form\n[Submit an enquiry](https://go.gov.sg/ease-feedback)\n\n## Phone number\nIf you require assistance with the application, you may visit any Community Centre (CC) or ServiceSG Centre. You may also call BCA's hotline  [1800-342-5222](tel:1800-342-5222).\n\nIf you wish to obtain hard copy EASE (Private) vouchers, you may visit any Community Centre islandwide and they would assist you to print the vouchers.",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Disability support, Financial support and benefits, Housing and shelters\n\n# Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/SMF*\n\nProvides subsidies to seniors for mobility and assistive devices or home healthcare items.\n\n## Highlights\n- Up to 90% subsidy for mobility and assistive devices (e.g. wheelchairs, hearing aids)\n- Up to 80% subsidies for home healthcare items (e.g. milk feeds, adult diapers)\n- Approach your therapist or AIC directly to apply\n\n**Who it targets:** Persons with disabilities, Seniors\n**Keywords:** Assistive devices, Home healthcare, Seniors\n\n## About this support\nTo support ageing in place, you may apply for the following subsidies for seniors who live at home:\n\n- Subsidies of up to 90% for approved mobility and assistive devices (e.g. mobility aids such as walking/quad stick, wheelchair, geriatric chair, commodes, pressure relief mattress/cushions, hospital beds, spectacles, hearing aids, etc.)\n- Subsidies of up to 80% for approved home healthcare items (e.g. milk feeds, diapers, etc.)\n\n## Who is this for?\n- 60 years old and above\n- Singapore Citizen or PR\n- Monthly household income per capita of less than or equal to $4,800 (or property annual value of $21,000 or below for households with no income)\n- Pass a [means-test](https://aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Seniors-Mobility-and-Enabling-Fund---Mobility-and-Assistive-Devices#faq) for Intermediate and Long-Term Care (ILTC) services\n- Seniors and persons with disabilities will be served under one scheme and agency throughout their lifetime\n- If the individual has tapped on Assistive Technology Fund (ATF)^ before the age of 60, they will continue to be served by ATF throughout their lifetime and not SMF\n- If the individual has not tapped on ATF subsidies before the age of 60, they would be served by SMF throughout their lifetime\n- Individuals can approach their care provider, e.g. hospitals, community care organisations, social service agencies, to enquire about their eligibility for the schemes\n- They may also approach the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) if they are not currently receiving support from any care provider\n\n^ATF provides subsidies for persons with disabilities (PWDs) to purchase the assistive technology devices to enable independent living\n\nAdditional criteria for assistive devices:\n\n- Assessed by a qualified assessor to require the device\n- Must not reside in a nursing home or sheltered home\n\nAdditional criteria for motorised devices:\n\n- Must not have a full-time caregiver or domestic worker\n- Unable to use a manual wheelchair independently\n- Assessed to be mentally and physically able to safely use the motorised device\n\nAdditional criteria for home healthcare items:\n\n- Must not be a current recipient of subsidies for the same items\n- Must be receiving Home Nursing, Home Medical, Home Palliative Care, or Day Hospice services\n\n## How to apply?\nYou can apply:\n\n- via the therapist or social worker at the hospital, day rehabilitation centre, or senior care centre from which your loved one is receiving care\n- online [using Singpass](https://for.sg/smf-application-using-singpass) or [without Singpass](https://for.sg/smf-application-not-using-singpass)\n- By mailing the [completed application form for assistive device or mobility device](http://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/SMF-Application-Form.pdf) and supporting documents to Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF), No. 7 Maxwell Road #04-01, MND Complex Annex B, Singapore 069111\n\nYou'll need to provide:\n\n- Copy of Applicant's NRIC (front and back) or a copy of the digital NRIC available on SingPass\n- For first time application for motorised device, doctor memo or [Need for Assessment form](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/Cerification-of-Medical-Need-Form.pdf) indicating need for motorised device must be submitted.\n- Copies of medical reports, if available\n- Copies of financial assistance documents, if available\n\n## Where to go\n[Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/about-us/aic-link)\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.aic.sg/financial-assistance/seniors-mobility-enabling-fund)\n\n## Email / Form\n[Submit an enquiry](https://www.aic.sg/About-Us/Contact-Us-Form)\n\n## Phone number\nAIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:1800-650-6060)",

    "embedding_text": "Domains: Active Ageing, Caregiving support, Disability support, Family, parenting and relationships, Healthcare and well-being\n\n# Healthy 365\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/schemes/HEALTHY365*\n\nHealthy 365 is a mobile application that helps resident to discover and access healthy lifestyle offerings that will help them to achieve their health goals.\n\n## Highlights\n- Self-directed programmes to engage residents to initiate and sustain healthy lifestyle behaviours\n- Real-time rewards for achieving desired healthy lifestyle behaviours\n- Download the Healthy 365 app from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store\n\n**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable\n**Keywords:** Resources and Support\n\n## About this support\n- Track your daily physical activity and sleep duration with a compatible wearable\n- Use the meal log tool to monitor your daily calorie intake\n- Participate in challenges such as the National Steps Challenge™ and Eat, Drink, Shop Healthy Challenge\n- Earn Healthpoints and redeem Healthpoints from a catalogue of lifestyle rewards\n- Participate in recommended programmes and booking activities, such as free exercise classes and health workshops.\n- Enjoy access to informative resources and partner programmes\n\n## Who is this for?\n- Singapore Citizens, Permanent Residents or Foreign Identification Number (FIN) holders aged 15 and above with a Singpass account\n\n## How to apply?\n- Download the Healthy 365 app on Apple Store / Google Play\n- Follow the on-screen steps to create a new account or log-in to your Healthy 365 app\n- You will need your Singpass account to sign up for a Healthy 365 account\n\n## Agency website\n[View more details](https://www.healthhub.sg/programmes/healthyliving)\n\n## Email / Form\n[Submit an enquiry](mailto:HPB_mailbox@hpb.gov.sg)\n\n## Phone number\nHPB hotline: [1800 223 1313](tel:1800-223-1313)\nOperating Hours: Mon -     "embedding_text": "Domains: Caregiving, Caregiving support, Legacy planning, Retirement and legacy planning\n\n# CPF Nomination\n\n*Source: https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/services/SVC-CPFN*\n\nAllows you to decide what happens to your CPF savings after your death.\n\n**Who it targets:** Families, Low-income, Persons with disabilities, Seniors, Vulnerable\n**Citizenship:** SG, PR\n**Keywords:** Advance Care Planning, Free\n\n## About this support\nA CPF nomination allows you to decide:\n\n- Who will receive your CPF savings (your “nominee”)\n- The percentage of your CPF savings each nominee should receive\n- CPF savings **cannot be distributed by a will **as CPF savings do not form part of your estate. This arrangement **protects your CPF savings from creditor claims** on any outstanding debts you may have and preserves your savings fully for your nominees.\n\nYour CPF nomination will cover:\n\n- CPF savings in your Ordinary, Special, MediSave and Retirement Accounts\n- CPF LIFE premium balance\n- Your discounted Singtel shares (if any)\n\nYour CPF nomination does not cover:\n\n- Properties bought using your CPF savings\n- Payout from the Dependants' Protection Scheme (DPS)\n- Investments under CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS)\n\n## Who is this for?\nTo make a CPF nomination, you must:\n\n- Be a CPF member\n- Be aged 16 years and above\n- Have the mental capacity to make your own decisions\n\nYou can **nominate any person or legal entity*** to be the beneficiary of your CPF savings.\n\n*An entity that is capable of receiving monies in its own right.\n\n## How to apply?\nYou can:\n\n- Apply [online](http://cpf.gov.sg/MakeCPFNOM) using your Singpass\n- [Make an appointment](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/appt/oas/form) to apply in person at any CPF service centre if you are unable to find two witnesses\n- [Book an appointment](https://www.booking.gov.sg/public/services/G4x7rneZ/list) to visit a [ServiceSG Centre](https://mylegacy.life.gov.sg/find-a-service/life-planning-service/) for in-person guidance on your online nomination application. Click [here](https://www.psd.gov.sg/servicesg/) for the list of ServiceSG Centres and their operating hours\n\n**For online application**\n\nYou will need to have:\n\n**Your nominees’ particulars**\n\n1. Full Name\n2. NRIC or Foreign Identification Number (FIN)\n3. Mailing Address (for foreigners)\n4. Email Address (optional)\n\n**Two witnesses’ particulars**\n\n1. Full Name\n2. NRIC\n3. Email address and/or Singapore-registered mobile phone number\n4. Cannot be a nominee\n5. He/she cannot be a nominee and must be at least 21 years of age\n\nUpon submission of your nomination,** inform your witnesses to log in **[here](http://cpf.gov.sg/witnessNOM)** within 7 calendar days to witness your nomination using their Singpass.**\n\n**For in-person application**\n\nYou will need to bring along and prepare:\n\n- A copy of your NRIC/passport\n- Your nominee(s)' NRIC number or Foreign Identification Number (FIN), email (optional), and mailing address (for foreigners)\n\nAs CPF Board's customer service executives or ServiceSG staff are acting as your witnesses, you do not need to prepare your witnesses' particulars.\n\n## What to expect?\nIf your nominee falls into the following categories, here is what to expect:\n\n**Below 18 Years Old**\nThe monies will be held in trust by the Public Trustee until your nominee turns 18.\n**Unable To Make Decisions Independently**\nThe monies will be handled by their court appointed deputy.\n**Bankrupt**\nThe monies belonging to the undischarged bankrupt nominee, will be transferred to the Official Assignee.\n\nTo allow your CPF savings to be distributed swiftly according to your wishes when you pass on, it is important to **review your CPF nomination regularly**, especially at key milestones (e.g.):\n\n- Starting Work\n- Marriage*\n- Childbirth\n- Divorce\n- Death of a nominee\n- When you reach your golden years**\n\n*Your nomination will be revoked upon marriage, and you should make a new nomination.\n\n**Review your nomination and consider your current family circumstances, such as which family member may need your savings more.",
